Paul failed to pass his A-levels at school, achieving only in Art. He took a foundation course in Art and Design at Loughborough Art College. He then failed to be accepted onto a Fine Art Degree course, and failed again the following year to gain a place on a Furniture Design course. He retook his A-levels, doing evening classes at the technical college. With some newfound determination, he got the grades he needed and gleefully embarked on a degree in Product Design. Paul graduated from Loughborough University in 1987 with a 2:1 and co-founded Insight Design Consultancy.

The business failed to win enough commissions in a recession and folded in its second year. Paul and two of the partners tried their hand at restoring classic cars, but it soon became clear that the task required many years of experience in mechanics and panel beating. They ended up selling Austin Healey wrecks to an Italian car restorer and supplying parts. With that business also floundering because of the lack of available stock, the partners, Paul, Phil deVries and Will Jameson decided they had one more chance before accepting that they would need to get a proper job, so they each went home for the weekend to think of something.

Phil’s idea was the best: restore and sell antique pine furniture. They all agreed this could work, Paul even had some experience working at The Old Pine Shop in Ross on Wye over a couple of summers. Their first sale was a flop, only one person turned up, a neighbour interested to see what was going on. Completely broke, Paul put a desperate ad in the local paper: “Half price door stripping, £5 per door, no VAT.” For the first time, the phone was ringing, and they were collecting doors from nearby Leicester, Nottingham and Derby. Often loading the first tank at 6am, and spraying down the last doors at midnight, they were stripping 60 doors a day from a rented garage. Clambering around atop a caustic tank, sinking doors clad in overalls, gas mask, gauntlets and wellies, it was a horrible job, but they were happy, they were making ends meet for the very first time.

Will saw sense and got an actual graduate job, leaving Paul and Phil to follow their dream of stripping enough doors to buy some woodworking machinery to do what they really wanted, which was to make their own furniture.

With a £600 80-year-old Wadkin table saw and a £150 Wadkin morticer, equally ancient, they made their first piece of furniture, a Welsh dresser commissioned by Paul’s Mum. The business moved to a 2,000 sq ft workshop, down an alleyway on Baxtergate in Loughborough, where they set up a stripping room, a workshop with 5 carpenter's benches, and a display area to show their wares. With restored pieces of antique pine furniture, alongside farmhouse-style tables that they had made, they started taking one-off commissions, until one day they decided to cut the middle drawer out of a dresser base and replace it with a Belfast sink. The first deVOL sink cabinet was born, and bespoke pine kitchen commissions followed. 'deVOL' being an amalgamation of Phil deVries and Paul O’Leary’s surnames, and coincidentally, LOVed backwards.

In 1998, with the business barely able to pay the rent, Phil decided to leave and buy a small holding in Portugal with his wife. He came back many years later to earn extra money, and now works 40 weeks of the year at Cotes Mill, managing all the works on the estate.

On his own, Paul was nervous, so he decided to downsize, moving to a small shop in the village of Quorn, where he planned to make furniture from the back room and live upstairs. But, as soon as he put some posters of their work in the window, they suddenly had a new clientele. The affluent villages nearby had budgets Paul could only dream of, homeowners happy to spend £5,000 on a kitchen. Instead of downsizing, Paul increased the number of carpenters, gave up the stripping, and specialised in designing and making kitchens full-time.

Paul tells this story to encourage budding entrepreneurs to never give up; multiple failures do not make you a failure.

deVOL now employs 400 staff, has showrooms in Leicestershire, London, Bath, New York and Los Angeles. Along with Managing Director, Robin McLellan and Creative Director, Helen Parker, deVOL made two TV series for the Discovery Channel, 'For The Love of Kitchens', both series receiving Emmy nominations, and now shown all around the world.

Paul’s dream was to one day run a modern-day Bauhaus, where designers and makers from every discipline work under one roof to create household wares that were as close to perfect as possible, but in an old-fashioned way. The deVOL style still reflects the detail and proportion that Paul and Phil experienced restoring old pine furniture in the late 80s. You can read the whole sorry story in 'The deVOL Kitchen', published by Penguin Random House.

Robin started a one year placement at deVOL in 2005 and returned as a permanent member of staff after completing his degree in Industrial Design and Technology at Loughborough University with a First Class Honours degree.

Robin started selling his wood turnings at a shop in Worcester at the age of ten. By the age of twenty, Robin had acquired an extensive home workshop, including two lathes. He has an incredible knowledge of the properties of even quite rare timbers, as well as a thorough knowledge of traditional carpentry techniques.

With the practical skills he has at his disposal, Robin quickly became a highly regarded member of our design & development team and became influential in streamlining production, working closely with Ben Creed. He also ensured that each cabinet met our specifications to minute tolerances.

Robin was promoted to Production Manager in 2008 and to a share­holding Managing Director in 2011. From the moment Robin walked into my shop as a student with an oar sticking out of a hold-all, he has never ceased to impress. Robin is as ambitious and dedicated as he is talented and trustworthy. deVOL kitchens Ltd will no doubt continue to flourish as Robin slowly but surely takes responsibility for everything that makes deVOL special; the most important being our staff, who are an exceptional bunch of creative, honest and hardworking people.

Robin’s interests include renovating property, white water kayaking and building vintage motorcycles.

Helen joined deVOL as a Kitchen Designer in 2004 after a lengthy sabbatical raising a family, she quickly proved that she has the wherewithal to guide prospective clients through the kitchen design process.

Helen was promoted to the position of Creative Director in 2011 after showing an innate ability to forecast trends and give deVOL a style direction. She was given the task of redesigning deVOL's kitchen displays both at Cotes Mill and our first London showroom, this included designing new pieces of furniture to add to our existing Classic and Shaker ranges. One of our favourite of Helen’s designs is the beautiful deVOL Curiosity cupboard which launched in 2016 and has already become a firm favourite with our customers. Designed with the ‘old museum’ cabinets in mind, this piece is simple, functional and works in just about every room of your home.

Although Helen no longer designs kitchens directly for our customers, she oversees and helps with the training of all deVOL’s kitchen designers both at Cotes Mill and in London and is still very involved with all aspects of the kitchen design service.

deVOL’s easy, cool and understated style is Helen's inspiration and her original approach to our look is quite unique. Over the last thirteen years that Helen has been with the company it has changed from a small Leicestershire business, to a household name. Helen's passion and desire to create a special look for deVOL has proved to be the making of this company.

She works with Tim, our photographer, on all the styling and imagery for the company, organising photoshoots both in-house and in customers’ homes. deVOL’s timeless, original and impeccably styled photography is one of the key things which have helped us to become such a well regarded name in the design and interiors industry.

Helen is also involved with the design and writing of text for all deVOL brochures and advertising, regularly being asked to submit editorials for local and national magazines and newspapers such as Elle Decoration, Homes & Gardens, Livingetc and The Sunday Times, she has become a voice of knowledge when it comes to interiors and stylish living.

When we design new kitchen ranges and work on collaborations and new projects Helen is a key member of the deVOL Design Team. Her amazing eye for style and knack for getting things just spot on were very important in the design and launch of our Sebastian Cox Kitchen range in 2015, which has gone on to win multiple awards for its unique urban rustic look.

Helen is also responsible for styling, sourcing and buying all the antiques and gifts on display here at the Mill and has introduced an exciting and eclectic range of products old and new. As well as sourcing products from all over the world, Helen has been working closely with our deVOL potter and ceramicist to create a small but growing collection of classic stoneware in the most beautiful soft muted colours, the pieces are practical and simple and they will be around forever.

Most recently, Helen has been responsible for designing our incredible new London showroom and townhouse in the historic square of St. John, Clerkenwell. A design that has already got the media and interiors world talking; with soft pink and green walls, cupboards painted in our new ‘Clerkenwell Blue’, a wall covered in our very own dark green metro style deVOL tiles, oil paintings hanging from the walls, quirky palm trees and houseplants, antique chandeliers and kooky Majolica pottery, Helen’s brave and inspired choices have created an evocative and carefully considered space in which to display our bespoke Classic English cupboards.

Helen is a keen blogger and is always actively ensuring deVOL and its image is kept classic, on trend and eclectic. She loves food, unusual ingredients, exploring markets and local restaurants, spending time gardening and watching world movies. Helen’s hobbies are a kind of extension of her work at deVOL, all of the things Helen loves are a part of her job. She is hoping to get the deVOL food truck up and running this year and create a lovely vegetable garden at the Mill too; all of these things are intrinsically linked to her home life in the loveliest way.

Paul studied Industrial Design and Technology at Loughborough University, graduating with a 2:1 in 2013. During his studies he took a placement year job where he helped to produce products, merchandise and furniture for Coca-Cola for use at the London Olympics.

After graduating, Paul worked for a small product design consultancy where he worked on a diverse range of products from high-tech medical products all the way to coffee packaging.

Paul joined deVOL and began working at Cotes Mill to learn the ropes as a Kitchen Designer. He then moved to the Tysoe Street, London showroom in September 2015 where he undertook the role of Assistant Manager. Paul quickly worked his way up to become Manager of the Tysoe Street showroom, and in June 2017 moved over to manage deVOL's amazing St. John's Square showroom and townhouse.

In April 2019, Paul made the move to New York to become the manager of deVOL’s new Bond Street showroom in Manhattan, as well as spending time designing the most beautiful kitchens for our lovely customers. In 2023, Paul was made deVOL's US Sales Director. Since then Paul has moved back to the UK but remains our US Sales Director, managing the US side of the business as well as overseeing the Bond Street showroom. His friendly personality, impeccable organisational skills and passion for design make him the absolute perfect person for this job. 

Paul is a very active person. He has swam competitively at a national level, played for Loughborough University’s water polo 1st's team and has taken to competing in triathlons since finishing university. Most of his holidays revolve around skiing, golf or tennis.

Annah graduated from Nottingham Trent University in 2017, specialising in Furniture & Product Design. Once graduated, Annah joined deVOL at Cotes Mill and after learning the ins and outs, she moved to join the team at the St. John's Square, London showroom in November 2017.

In 2022, Annah flew across the pond to join the New York team as a Senior Kitchen Designer and in 2023, became Bond Street's Design Manager. While working on her own projects with clients all over the States, Annah also oversees designs for the rest of the team.

Outside of work, Annah is training for the New York marathon and exploring different parts of the city. Using New York as a base for more travelling, Annah has made recent trips to California and Iceland and is currently planning her next adventure!

Elise graduated from Sheffield Hallam University in 2009 with a 2:1 in Early Childhood Studies, with a focus on development, inclusion, and the health and culture of children. This gave her the chance to experience a variety of early years settings as well as the opportunity to spend 6 weeks working in a school and orphanage in Mumbai.

Although she will always have a passion for working with children, her career path shifted when she became a Brand Development Manager for the luxury interior brands Sanderson, William Morris & Co, Zoffany, and Harlequin. Being surrounded by beautiful fabrics and wallpaper sparked her interest in interiors and design, something she used in her personal life to renovate and design her own house. This passion for interiors and design then transitioned to a professional career when she started working for deVOL as a Design Coordinator.

In her spare time, Elise enjoys spending time in nature, camping or keeping active, by climbing, running or attempting to surf! She’s a keen cook and has been enjoying the chance to explore all the great food spots that London has to offer, but most weekends you will find her escaping the city in search of the best wild swim spots.

Corbin graduated from Brigham Young University in Utah in 2021 with a degree in Industrial Design. One of his final, and favourite, projects involved designing and selling bar stools made from beautiful reclaimed wood from a local barn. 

Corbin joined deVOL as a Kitchen Designer and helps the design team with all customer projects, as well as being a very friendly face around the showroom. 

He loves language and travel and spent two and a half years living abroad completing his religious mission in the Balkans, studying biology in South Africa, studying global leadership and engineering in the UK and studying design in the Netherlands.

In his spare time, Corbin loves baking, photography, playing the guitar and hiking in national parks. He is also currently training for his first ultra marathon, 100 miles long!

Phoebe graduated from Nottingham Trent University in 2020 after studying for her BA (Hons) in Furniture and Product Design.

Phoebe grew up doing art and crafts, slowly refining her passion over the years through school, university, design competitions and working at her family's pottery business. These experiences, alongside working for a bespoke kitchen company at university, meant she was keen to pursue a career in the design industry. As a Kitchen Designer at deVOL, Phoebe loves to combine a mixture of our accessories and antiques throughout the kitchen to provide our customers with a beautiful and functional space they can spend all day relaxing in. After joining deVOL and working at Cotes Mill, Phoebe moved to join the team at the Bond Street, New York showroom in 2022.

When not designing, Phoebe likes to explore new areas, including discovering new live music venues and comedy shows across New York. When not exploring the city, she likes to brew her own wine, read and cook delicious new recipes!

Emily studied at Brigham Young University with a BFA in Industrial Design where she was awarded IDSA's Student Merit Award. She then went on to get a MA degree in Design Research, Writing and Criticism at the School of Visual Arts in New York. Emily's senior project was a board game designed to help children learn better communication skills within guided counselling programmes. 

After graduating, Emily completed an internship with a furniture and lighting company in the Netherlands, before returning to her hometown in Utah and working as a graphic designer for a film studio. Emily joined the NYC deVOL team as a Kitchen Design Assistant in 2023. Her role involves helping the other designers with their projects by drawing up lots of lovely deVOL kitchens and assisting in design meetings. Emily also takes on her own projects and is always a helping hand around the showroom. 

Outside of work, Emily is heavily involved in the art community - she curates shows, does ceramics, paints and writes poetry. She has recently gotten into film photography and is interested in putting a book together of all her poems and photos. When she's not being creative, you may find Emily hunting down the best NYC food spots. Her parents owned a restaurant so she loves to go out and try new dishes!

Gabrielle graduated from the University of North Carolina in Chapel Hill with a degree in Elementary Education, leading her to teach mathematics for seven years in Washington D.C. and New York City. Gabrielle then decided to return to school to study Interior Design where she graduated with Presidential Honours. During these studies, Gabrielle had a class focused on kitchen design where she fell in love with this aspect of design.

In 2023 Gabrielle joined the NYC team as a Kitchen Design Assistant and in 2025 was promoted to become a Kitchen Designer. Gabrielle has worked on a wide range of wonderful kitchen projects of all shapes and sizes across the US. Gabrielle works closely with the design team and customers, discussing designs, preparing drawings, and bringing thoughtful attention to detail on each and every project.

Growing up in Salt Lake City, Utah, Gabrielle developed a love of hiking, snowboarding and just generally being outdoors. When travelling, Gabrielle often looks for places where she can enjoy the landscape and spend time outside exploring - her most recent holiday was to Kauai, Hawaii! Gabrielle also enjoys running, sewing, cooking, exploring New York's restaurant scene and admiring the city's beautiful architecture.

Alexa graduated from the University of Nottingham in 2012 with a 2:1 degree in Architectural Studies. After realising that architecture wasn’t the right path for her, she chose to focus on her favourite room in the house: the kitchen.

Following four years as a Kitchen Designer, Alexa joined the deVOL team as Assistant Manager of the Tysoe Street showroom. In 2017, she was promoted to Manager, where she oversaw the day-to-day running of the London showroom and enjoyed guiding customers through the kitchen design process.

In October 2025, Alexa made the exciting move to the West Coast to become the Showroom and Design Manager of our Los Angeles showroom. Alexa oversees all our wonderful projects here, as well as working on her own designs for customers, and ensures the showroom runs seamlessly.

Outside of work, Alexa enjoys visiting art exhibitions and spending time eating and drinking with friends and family. She’s also a keen traveller and is always planning her next sunny getaway.

Claire joined deVOL after graduating from Loughborough University with a First Class Honours in 3D Design, specialising in ceramics.

For her final project, Claire worked alongside deVOL to create a collection of functional kitchenware that explored simple and utilitarian forms with a focus on coloured clay to add a contemporary twist. She was awarded first prize for Enterprise and Innovation at her degree show, as well as the ‘New Designer of the Year - Runner Up’ at the New Designers 2016 exhibition in London.

Claire began working at Cotes Mill in the summer of 2016, just as the ceramics department was starting up. She was responsible for developing and making the tableware ranges, as well as producing our tiles and pendant lights. As the studio grew and more products were introduced, Claire began overseeing the day-to-day running of the ceramics department, ensuring that deVOL’s high standards of craftsmanship were maintained from start to finish, as well as working on new products with our directors and product design team.

In October 2025, Claire moved to LA to become the Showroom Manager and Project Coordinator of our showroom in West Hollywood. She now oversees the smooth running of the showroom and is the first point of contact for anyone interested in working with deVOL on a project.

Outside of work, Claire enjoys staying active - she’s a keen cyclist, runner, and swimmer - but will never say no to a pint at the pub!

Millie graduated from Nottingham Trent University in the summer of 2021 with a 2:1 in Product Design. For her final year project, Millie created a design ‘Pebble’, which aimed to enhance the mental health and wellbeing of healthcare staff throughout the Covid-19 pandemic. This piece went on to be selected as part of the The Lost Graduation show in Milan in September 2021.

Having spent her placement year working in sustainable contract furniture, Millie went on to design luxury and bespoke sofas and chairs before joining deVOL in November 2022. This experience with high-end furniture meant she was perfectly placed to join the incredible team of kitchen designers at our Tysoe Street showroom in London.

Millie made the move over to the West Coast in October 2025 to become a Senior Kitchen Designer at our showroom in Los Angeles. She loves meeting with our customers and drawing up beautiful plans for their new spaces.

In her free time, Millie enjoys exploring LA with friends and finding new places to eat, as well as playing tennis at the weekends.

Isabel joined deVOL after graduating from Loughborough University in 2022 with a degree in Industrial Design and Technology. In the same year, Isabel won the Royal Society of Art Student Design award, earning her a fellowship and a feature in Wallpaper Magazine.

Having worked as an interior designer during her university placement year, Isabel began honing her interest in helping people create beautiful spaces in their own homes, leading her to deVOL. Isabel worked her way up from assistant to Senior Kitchen Designer over three years at our St John's Square showroom in London. She then made the move to Los Angeles in October 2025 as part of the team tasked with opening our new base on the West Coast. Isabel has really enjoyed getting to know lots of lovely new customers since moving to LA, and can't wait to see more of her kitchen designs come to life.

When she's not at work, Isabel loves catching the sunrise on the beach in Santa Monica in the mornings and keeping active, especially with an early Sunday morning hike! Making the most of the wide variety of food in LA, Isabel has been particularly keen on sampling the famous street tacos around the city and a plethora of great sushi spots! So far, she's not missing rainy London!

Edward studied Architecture with Environmental Design at the University of Nottingham, graduating in 2021 with a First Class Degree. During his studies, Edward developed a passion for designing sensitive and welcoming spaces, with a rigorous examination of building materials and the embodied and sequestered carbon related to them. At university, Edward won a competition to design and build a pavilion at Wirksworth Art Festival using reclaimed pallets. Edward’s final year thesis project, a bamboo pavilion, went on to be constructed in the Milton Keynes Council office.

Some other exciting projects Edward has been involved with include creating and running a VR environment at TEDx Bath for Yasmeen Lari's humanitarian housing project in Pakistan, as well as designing and building installations in both 2022 and 2023 for the Forest of Imagination Art Festival in Bath.

Here at deVOL, Edward is part of our Project Management team, first working in Leicestershire and then moving over to sunny LA in 2025. Working closely with our Kitchen Designers, Edward guides our customers from 2D drawings to fully completed kitchen cupboards, ensuring each detail has been thought through and works beautifully in practice.  

In his free time, Edward enjoys furniture making and fine woodworking, using reclaimed wood and predominantly hand tools. Creations have included coffee tables, play shelves for his nephew and items for his workshop. Edward also likes to go climbing outdoors and taking long country walks.

Katie graduated from Nottingham Trent University in 2009, specialising in print and embroidery; her style focused on graphical line drawings of iconic London imagery. Soon after graduating Katie started working in our flooring business, Floors of Stone Ltd. Katie was excellent with customers and gained expertise in all aspects of sales, logistics and customer service. Katie became office supervisor as the business grew, until she was offered a place on the kitchen design team at deVOL. Katie had always been interested in interior design, so the move satisfied her desire to use her creative skills in her job. Katie quickly got up to speed designing on CAD and guiding clients through the kitchen design process.

In 2015 Katie was appointed as Head Kitchen Designer, her friendly and approachable personality, design flair and impeccable organisational skills made her the perfect person for this job. She now works closely with our team of designers at the Mill, discussing their projects and helping each designer create the very best and most practical design for their customer’s space.

Katie likes to have a good nosey at all of the potential projects we receive on a daily basis, but the best bit is seeing photographs of the finished rooms and hearing from happy customers who love their new kitchens.

Although Katie spends most of her time helping our team of designers, she still enjoys having her own kitchen clients when she can, there’s nothing better than working closely with a customer and seeing a project through from beginning to end. The Kew and Bath Shaker kitchens are a couple of Katie’s favourite projects that she has worked on. Not only were the customers lovely, making the design process a dream, but the finished kitchens look so clean and beautiful. Simple designs always make the best ones.

Katie loves working at Cotes Mill, being surrounded by friendly and creative people and working in a place where there’s always something new going on. She especially likes seeing all of the new ceramics coming out of our little studio and is looking forward to the very first deVOL jewellery collection. Katie has just bought a new house, which needs some serious renovating, so she can now totally relate to customers in a similar position!

In her spare time she likes to sew, print and makes her own furnishings, most recently, she has started making paper-mache lights, a very messy process but rewarding in the end! Travelling is another of Katie’s passions, with her favourite destinations so far being the USA, Canada, Berlin and Stockholm.

Helen studied 3D Design at Loughborough University, graduating in 2013 with a 2:1 in 3D design. Shortly after graduating, Helen joined deVOL as a Kitchen Designer at the Cotes Mill headquarters and in September 2017 made the big move down to London to become a member of the design team in our Tysoe Street showroom. She has since returned back to Leicestershire to work at Cotes Mill.

Before joining deVOL, Helen worked as an assistant at The Lightbox Gallery, The Eden Project and also spent time teaching as a volunteer in Sri Lanka. Alongside her degree, Helen also undertook internships with product and furniture designer Michael Marriott and at Next in their homeware department.

Not only does Helen spend her days designing deVOL Kitchens, but she also helps to train our new Kitchen Designers, teaching them everything they need to know to design a practical, beautiful space that fulfils the customers’ needs and upholds deVOL’s principals and aesthetics. Discovering the things that our new staff excel in, as well as the things they find a little trickier, and helping them to grow in confidence in all aspects of their job is something Helen finds really rewarding.

Helen’s favourite project that she has worked on so far is The Peckham Rye Kitchen, a wonderfully bold, daring and eccentric room and the most talked about deVOL Kitchen ever. This space was different to anything Helen had ever designed before and it reminded her that the most challenging projects are always the best and the most rewarding.

If Helen had to pick one of her kitchen designs that she would most like to have in her own home, it would be The Park Kitchen Nottingham. It’s such a light and bright and open space with so many interesting details like the little round window seat and wonderfully high ceilings. The perfect mix of practical fitted furniture and freestanding bits and bobs, this kitchen is a delight and also features a retro Smeg fridge, something Helen has dreamed of having ever since she was little!

Helen’s absolute favourite thing about working at deVOL is all the lovely people she gets to work with, as well as having the opportunity to meet lots of interesting customers and help them to create lovely kitchens that they will get to enjoy for many years to come.

In her spare time, Helen loves doing lots of creative things. Since specialising in paper folding design in her final year at university, she’s been a bit obsessed with origami and making decorations, homewares and cards out of waste paper. Helen is also passionate about going to church and getting involved with volunteering projects. At the moment she is volunteering with a night shelter that her church helps to run in London, this is something Helen has always wanted to do.

Francesca graduated in 2017 with a 1st class honours degree in 3D Design: New Practice from Loughborough University. She harbours an innate passion for the Arts and has worked as a creative across the creative industries in Eindhoven, NL and the United Kingdom. During her time in Eindhoven, Francesca worked on humanitarian design projects at Hassani Design BV and at Studio Nacho Carbonell, Eindhoven, leading a small team of interns in the creation and manufacture of surreal, sculptural artworks and furniture pieces using a diverse range of materials and processes.

In London, Francesca worked as Studio Manager of Kennedy Woods Architecture, a rapidly growing Architecture studio in the heart of Peckham, where she gained experience in 2D CAD drawing, interior design, and furniture specification. In her hometown of Lincolnshire, Francesca has helped to pioneer numerous creative endeavours to encourage interest in and engagement with the Arts across the county.

Francesca joined deVOL as a Kitchen Designer in 2017. She loves to get to know her clients and designs every kitchen to perfectly suit each customer's individual needs and tastes. Francesca's sense of style is influenced by her nomadic lifestyle, growing up in fields, up mountains, or on horseback, and trawling Lincolnshire's treasure-filled antique shops for gems. She loves to be at one with nature and is most at home covered in dirt with her dog Peanut.

Emma graduated from De Montfort University in 2008 with a degree in Furniture Design. She joined deVOL towards the end of 2014. Her role focuses on drawing up customers kitchen plans and guiding them through the design process turning their ideas and requirements into their dream kitchen. Prior to working for deVOL she worked in Liverpool as an Interior Designer where she enjoyed working on a variety of projects and gained a greater understanding and love of interiors.

Emma has a passion for cooking and travel and loves to experience new foods and cultures. She is also an avid viewer of The Great British Bake Off and enjoys recreating what has been baked on the show. In her spare time Emma loves being outside and enjoys visiting the Lake District to go on walks. Having recently purchased her first home, Emma can't wait to take on the project of re-designing the interiors.

After graduating from Buckinghamshire New University, Hannah Joined deVOL as a Kitchen Designer at our Cotes Mill showrooms. During her time at university her designs were chosen to exhibit at both May Design Series 2015 and New Designers 2016.

Hannah has worked with a number of Public Art Groups including ‘Future City’ and ‘Public Works’ and has been a part of projects, such as ‘A Masterclass in Sitting’ and the ‘Last Chair Arch of High Wycombe’. She also won a public seating competition in 2015 commissioned by Berkley Homes, in partnership with Future City, Public Works and High Wycombe Council.

As a big fan of craft and wood working, Hannah enjoys learning about and experimenting with a whole range of materials and even specialised in the use of alternative materials in her final year at university.

Hannah also loves to fill her home with an eclectic mix of handmade, one-off ornaments and furniture.

Josephine studied Fashion Communications at Northumbria University where she particularly enjoyed exhibition design and visual merchandising. Before joining deVOL as a Kitchen Designer, she worked at as a Visual Merchandiser and then as an Interior Designer. Josephine’s best experience so far has been working in Älmhult, Sweden, on an exhibition that focused on the new home furnishing products for the coming year. She loved discovering the identity of Swedish design and getting inspired by the amazing shops in Malmö and Copenhagen.

Now, she loves creating beautiful and functional kitchens for deVOL’s customers that reflect the period and style of the property.

In her spare time, Josephine enjoys walking in the Peak District with her dog, Fenton, Interior Design and styling, shopping for antiques and going on holiday to Northumberland.

Lucy graduated from Nottingham Trent University in 2018 with a First Class Honours degree in Fashion Management, where she attained a knowledge of the retail market and business strategies. Whilst completing her degree, Lucy also gained her Diploma in Professional Practice and her dissertation was selected to be shown at Graduate Fashion Week.

In April 2021, Lucy joined the team at deVOL's historic Cotes Mill home as an Assistant Kitchen Designer. This role includes assisting the senior designers in every aspect of creating beautiful kitchens for our customers all over the world, including working on the room layout and design elevations, as well as putting together itemised quotations.

From a young age, Lucy has enjoyed drawing and designing. In 2014, she won first prize in the ISA Area & National Art Competition. Since then, she has developed her love for design, including upcycling antique pieces of furniture.

In her free time, Lucy enjoys cooking and creating new recipes with her partner. A typical Sunday includes visiting her family, going on a long dog walk with their sausage dogs, Darcey and Belle, finished with a Sunday roast dinner.

James graduated in 2021 with a 2:1 in Product Design from Nottingham Trent University. He officially joined us at deVOL in 2021 as an Assistant Kitchen Designer, but he actually spent his university placement year working as a Production Assistant at deVOL's Shepshed workshop, specialising in our Sebastian Cox and Shaker furniture.

As a designer, his main interests lie within architecture and the built environment, in particular, small space design. For James’s major project at university, he designed and built a more affordable full-scale garden office in response to the COVID-19 pandemic and the cultural shift towards hybrid working. He recently sold this garden office, and it is now being used for a small business.

Growing up in rural Gloucestershire, James has a strong appreciation for the outdoors, gardening and sustainability/upcycling. He’s also a keen traveller, inter-railing around Europe and exploring the east coast of Australia in a campervan! When he’s not off on exciting trips he likes to keep active, running, swimming and playing golf and cricket.

Michael graduated with a 2:1 in Product Design from Nottingham Trent university in 2021. Using his artistic flair, he was able to take an innovative approach to solving the problems faced in design briefs.

Finding a way to bridge a keen interest for art and problem solving, Michael spent a year on placement in the kitchen design industry where he developed a strong interest in all things 'interiors'. Michael joined the deVOL team as a Kitchen Designer at our Cotes Mill showrooms in Leicestershire in 2021. Although a lot of the design process takes place behind a computer screen, Michael loves interacting with deVOL customers all over the world. He particularly enjoys being able to bring all the elements of a new kitchen together to create a space that is not only beautiful but functional too.

Art, particularly drawing portraits, is one of Michael's passions, as well as exercise and enjoying the outdoors. Cotes Mill is a constant source of inspiration and he feels very lucky to be able to enjoy the lush, sprawling grounds and countryside surrounding the historic building.

Having graduated with a BA (Hons) in Graphic Design from the University of Chester, Miranda realised that she wanted to take a more three-dimensional approach to design. She went on to complete her MA in Design, focusing on interiors and exploring how people interact with their surroundings in commercial environments.

Before joining deVOL, Miranda worked as a bathroom designer and visual merchandiser which taught her about creating cohesive design schemes that are functional and engaging. As a Kitchen Design Assistant at our Cotes Mill showroom, Miranda is there to offer support to and learn from our talented team. She also uses her technical skills to draw up designs and quotes for each of their projects. Miranda particularly loves working on homes with lots of character and enjoys creating designs that are sympathetic to the age and style of the property.

Having spent a lot of time walking in the Lake District and Lancashire, the countryside is a particular source of inspiration that she likes to bring into the home. Miranda also really enjoys city breaks where she can experience different cultures, cuisines, and architecture; her current favourite is Bruges.

Poppy joined deVOL in July 2023 after achieving her degree in Psychology (Educational and Developmental) from Nottingham Trent.

As an Assistant Design Coordinator, Poppy is responsible for booking our appointments and is one of the very first people our lovely customers will talk to when beginning a project. Poppy replies to initial enquiries, advises on our process, and collects all the information our kitchen designers need prior to a consultation.

In her spare time Poppy enjoys running and walking her dog, Alfie, to local cafés for coffee and lunch. Poppy is also a keen traveller and loves to take short city breaks around the world.

Barbara graduated from the University of Derby in 2020 with a degree in Interior Design. From there, Barbara joined an interior design studio in Leicester where she got to exercise her love for the more technical side of the industry. 

In April 2025, Barbara joined deVOL’s Cotes Mill showroom as a Design Coordinator. As the first point of contact for UK and overseas kitchen enquiries (big and small), Barbara fields emails and phone calls covering all sorts of topics, from general queries about our furniture and accessories to more technical questions about our cabinetry and design process. Day-to-day, Barbara liaises between our customers and designers, putting together approximate costs, booking in appointments and ensuring the deVOL team have all the information they need to get started on plans and quotations. 

Outside of work, Barbara is a house music DJ in Leicester and plays as a duo with her fiancé! She also loves running, hiking, painting, cooking over the top dinner parties and BBQs, as well as playing with her little dog, Boris.

settings.custom_text_hover_position: Showroom Manager and Senior Kitchen Designer
settings.staff_role: Showroom Manager and Senior Kitchen Designer
settings.staff_description:
Matteo graduated from Loughborough University in 2015 with a first class degree in Fine Art. During his final year, he designed a series of sculptures ranging in scale and size, which explored the materiality of wood, concrete and glass, some of which were added to Loughborough University's private collection.  Matteo's work has been exhibited across the country, and he was invited to exhibit his work at the Affordable Art Fair in Battersea in 2015.

After graduating, Matteo returned to Loughborough University as part of the marketing team for the engineering department, before joining deVOL in 2017 at their Cotes Mill showrooms as a Kitchen Designer. In June 2018 Matteo made the move down to London and is now designing kitchens from our Tysoe Street showroom, which is located just off the fabulous Exmouth Market.  

During his weekends off work, Matteo enjoys visiting friends and binging on good food! With a strong interest in crafts, he still makes sculptures in his spare time and has also recently purchased leather making tools as he is eager to learn a new skill!

Iain graduated in 2008 with a 2:1 from Falmouth University. He first worked in deVOL’s Creative Design Office from 2013; managing magazine advertising, updating websites, proof-reading brochures and also photographing floor tiles. Iain is now one of our kitchen designers based in the new London showroom. He is fascinated in the design process where a customer’s initial ideas become a finished kitchen design. After graduating Iain was involved in the Nottingham Arts scene, with a role as Digital Coordinator at Surface Gallery. Here he curated several exhibitions, including an international exhibition of short film, subject which he has a great interest in.

Iain's own art practice take cues from nature, with a strong grounding in Fine Art. A degree project combined photography stills and computer graphics to create an interactive point-and-click adventure game. Living in Cornwall gave the chance to dive regularly and learn underwater photography. A passion for travel also has helped produce a portfolio of photos in East Asia as well as a year teaching English in South Korea. Other hobbies include foraging wild mushrooms and cooking.

Kristina joined deVOL after graduating in 2019 with a First Class Honours degree in Textile Design. As part of her course, she studied abroad in Milan and completed an internship with THE UNSEEN, a material innovation R&D house based in London. As part of her final year at university, Kristina developed a collection of tactile interior surfaces inspired by minimalism and Scandinavian culture.

As a Kitchen Designer and coming from a background in textiles, Kristina really enjoys getting to know her clients and helping them choose the perfect colour and finishes for their new kitchen. The best part of the job for Kristina is hearing lovely feedback from her clients and seeing the final finished deVOL furniture looking beautiful in her customer's home.

In her spare time, Kristina enjoys cycling and visiting her parents in Scotland and taking her two Australian Shepherds, Maisie and Luna, on long dog walks in the Scottish countryside. Kristina also has Scandinavian roots and enjoys frequent trips to see her family in Norway and tries to go snowboarding whenever she gets the chance!

Sam graduated from Nottingham Trent University in 2020 following a four year Furniture and Product Design BA Honours degree, including the completion of a 13 month internship - project managing and designing bespoke fine English cabinetry with a cabinetmaker in Guildford. His dissertation explored defining ‘classic’ design, how and why individual perspectives differ and the importance and power that design can have. Sam’s final piece was a Shaker-inspired sideboard following principles of quality, craftsmanship and functionality. This piece caught the eye of the Conran Shop and was shortlisted at New Designers for the Conran Shop Design Award.

Sam joined deVOL in July 2020 at Cotes Mill where he worked for six months before joining the team at the St. John’s Square showroom, London.

Sam loves working with his customers, taking their initial ideas and developing these into beautiful spaces. He has always loved designing and making pieces of furniture and was fortunate enough to be awarded a Young Furniture Makers Design Prize (sponsored by the Furniture Makers’ Company) in 2016 for his final piece for Product Design A level, a folding table.

Sam has always been a keen artist and photographer and has exhibited his work in a number of venues. He also has a real passion for music and is an accomplished classically trained singer. He was a tenor scholar throughout his time at university and still performs regularly with choirs and as a soloist. In his spare time, Sam often travels to visit and catch up with friends and family across the UK.

Ella graduated from the University of Manchester in 2024, obtaining a degree in Architecture. During her final year, Ella’s work focussed on designing a library for a small, traditional cotton textile town in the North. The design was inspired by weaving sheds and how natural light enters spaces. This project was chosen to represent the university in a Dezeen article, and a model of Ella’s building was shortlisted in The MSA Modelmaking Awards, partnered with Stanton Williams.

In January 2025, Ella joined deVOL as a Kitchen Design Assistant at our beautiful St. John’s Square showroom in London. This role involves drawing up designs and quotes for our customers and assisting the team wherever they need it. Ella particularly enjoys working on projects with lots of character, especially heritage or listed buildings.

Outside of deVOL, Ella enjoys playing tennis with her family and competing in lacrosse matches at weekends. You can also find her exploring new restaurants and galleries around London, with a focus on textiles exhibitions.

Having taken a gap year where he worked for a youth work charity in London, Barny moved to Loughborough to study Mathematics and Physics in 2015. In his final year, he specialised in quantum and solid-state physics. Barny graduated in 2018 and went on to work in sales for a promotional products company in Leicester, before joining deVOL in May 2019.

Barny has worked in multiple departments across deVOL and is highly knowledgeable about every aspect of the business. Starting in the Logistics team, Barny coordinated the deliveries of deVOL furniture all over the country and the world. Following a year working with our incredibly talented kitchen fitters in London, Barny joined the St. John’s Square showroom in 2025 as a Kitchen Design Technician. Here, Barny assists the team by drawing up designs and checking their technical feasibility. You can also find Barny out on the road, carrying out site surveys at our customers’ homes.

Outside work, Barny is a keen musician and sportsman and loves to travel as well as spend time with his son, Theo, who was born at the end of 2025!

Megan graduated in 2017 from Oxford Brookes University with a degree in Interior Architecture.

Before joining deVOL, Megan worked as an in-house interior designer in private members clubs which she helped to set up in London, Hong Kong, Singapore and China.

In April 2022, Megan became part of our Tysoe Street, London team where she is training to be a Kitchen Designer. While assisting our design team with customer projects, Megan will learn everything she needs to know to design a functional and beautiful kitchen that both fulfills the customer's needs and upholds deVOL's design principles.

When Megan's not at work, she makes little lino prints and spends lots of time sketching and doodling, cooking for friends and family, running and swimming in the sea at any opportunity! An office full of cyclists here at deVOL has also encouraged Megan to get a bike, which she now commutes to work on every day.

Katie graduated from Nottingham Trent University with a First class honors degree in Decorative Arts, designing and creating lighting, homewares and jewellery. Her graduate collection was awarded Highly Commended at New Designers and labelled by Trend Bible as 'One to watch'. She exhibited at various galleries and shows across the country including Great Northern Contemporary Craft Fair and Lustre.

Following her degree collection’s success, Katie was one of four applicants accepted onto the YA Silversmithing programme in Sheffield completing orders and developing new products in her own studio.

Before joining deVOL as a Metalware Designer, she worked as an interior designer and visual merchandiser. She spent the last 2 years travelling across 12 countries and driving around Australia in her self renovated campervan. Out of work, Katie enjoys discovering cosy coffee shops and beautiful interiors, watching documentaries and planning her next trip away.

Guy joined deVOL in 2023 after achieving a 2:1 degree in Product Design from Bournemouth University. As part of his degree, Guy undertook a placement year at a small commercial kitchen company where he fostered his interest and understanding of kitchen design.

As a Kitchen Designer, Guy’s main responsibility is to support the team at Tysoe Street with a fascinating array of deVOL projects, assisting with drawing and quoting for new customers and learning from our experienced designers how to bring our customers' ideas to life.

Before joining deVOL, Guy worked as a ski instructor in Whistler, Canada and a chalet host in Val D'Isere, France so the mountains and the snow are a passion and big part of his life. In his spare time, Guy loves to immerse himself in the outdoors by playing golf and going on scenic walks with his cocker spaniel, Lola.

Ayesha studied Product Design & Technology at Loughborough University, graduating in 2016 with a 2.1. Following her degree, Ayesha worked as a kitchen designer for eight years before joining deVOL in 2024. Working from our Tysoe Street showroom in Clerkenwell, London, Ayesha enjoys transforming our customers' ideas into beautiful kitchen designs. 

In her spare time, Ayesha enjoys going on hikes and travelling with her husband. In 2023 they completed a challenging five-day trek in Patagonia. When she’s not out enjoying nature, Ayesha loves to spend time at home, reading and cooking new recipes or exploring the bars and restaurants of London.

Jack graduated from university with a degree in Computer Aided Product Design, with his final project focusing on methods of improving the surface finish on 3D printed parts.

In August 2019, Jack joined the deVOL team as a Kitchen Surveyor. This role sees Jack travel all over the UK to our lovely customers' homes, where he measures up their kitchens with true precision prior to installation to ensure a perfect fit each and every time. Old properties, wonky walls and unexpected structural changes on site are a common occurrence in kitchen projects, so Jack's skill and attention to detail is vital. Once the rooms are measured, Jack will then create the CAD drawings for our project management team before the furniture goes into production in our Leicestershire workshops.

Outside of work, Jack's hobbies include football and playing guitar.

Olivia graduated from Bath Spa University in 2024 with a degree in Interior Design. Whilst there, Olivia studied both residential and commercial projects, often working with the beautiful listed buildings synonymous with Bath. For her final project, Olivia designed a self-funded community restaurant, offering affordable or free fresh meals. 

In August 2025, Olivia joined deVOL’s Tysoe Street showroom in London’s bustling Exmouth Market. As a Showroom and Kitchen Design Assistant, Olivia ensures our furniture displays always look beautiful and tidy each day and helps the design team with their meetings by drawing up project plans and putting together quotations. 

When she’s not exploring new countries, Olivia loves to cook and find new places to eat around London with her friends.

Petra first joined deVOL in 2016 as Design Coordinator of our Tysoe Street showroom after graduating from Loughborough University with a degree in Textiles: Innovation and Design. Over the next four years, she transitioned into the role of Kitchen Designer and was a key part of the London team. In 2020, Petra left the big city to manage and run a boutique cafe in the West Wales countryside before moving to Bristol a few years later. It was perfect timing as we were just about to open our latest showroom in Bath and we were delighted by the idea of Petra coming back to deVOL as Showroom Manager at 17 George Street.

During renovations, Petra was one of our main people on site and was instrumental in making sure everything was set up and running smoothly for the showroom opening in October 2023. Her new role is focused on training, supporting and managing the Bath team to ensure we give the very best customer service and that the showroom displays are as beautiful as can be. She's always on hand to show customers around and chat about projects of all shapes and sizes, and is particularly excited to be designing kitchens for the incredible period houses around this beautiful city.

Outside of deVOL, Petra loves camping, wild swimming and road cycling. When she's not on an adventure, you'll most likely find her pottering around antique shops and searching for delicious artisan coffee or back at home renovating, painting walls and sewing accessories.

settings.staff_degree: BA (Hons) Textile Design for Fashion & Interiors
settings.staff_description:
Alice graduated from Bath Spa University in 2016, where she studied Textile Design, focussing on fashion and interiors. This passion for design and salvaged and pre-loved items led Alice to set up her own lifestyle shop, specialising in vintage handcrafted furniture and homeware.

In June 2023, Alice became one of our first new hires for our latest showroom in Bath. It was fantastic to have her on site ensuring everything was all set up before we were ready to open in October. In her role as Assistant Showroom Manager, Alice helps the day-to-day running of this magnificent place, booking in design appointments and making sure everyone who visits us has the best possible experience. She also really enjoys helping our lovely customers bring their ideas to life, drawing up plans and quotations for all sorts of different projects.

When she’s not at work, Alice is busy renovating her own Victorian terrace house, filling it with antique finds and her floristry creations, or taking a walk in the countryside with her partner and dog, Wesley.

Emma graduated with a degree in Business Administration where she studied an array of subjects from marketing, economics, strategy, logistics, accounting and more. After her studies, Emma began working in marketing but soon decided to follow her passion, retrain and pursue a career in interior design.

Whilst completing an interior design course at KLC School of Design, Emma worked at Little Greene as a colour advisor, before joining deVOL as a Junior Kitchen Designer in May 2022.

Emma began her deVOL career working from our historic St. John's Square townhouse in London before making the move down to Bath in October 2023, to be part of our amazing George Street team. Emma helps our design team with all customer kitchen projects, as well as showing visitors around and being a friendly and welcoming face in the showroom.

In her spare time, Emma loves cooking, painting and exploring new places, with past trips including a few months travelling around South America where she hiked and camped through the Andes.

Jordan joined deVOL in 2017 as a Kitchen Designer after graduating from Nottingham University with a 2:1 in Product Design. During his final year at university, Jordan designed and created products that utilised natural materials and made the most of both modern and traditional production methods. Jordan’s major project was a Shaker-inspired bar stool with a hidden rotating seat mechanism, designed to add functionality and comfort to a traditional bar stool without taking away from its natural, simplistic beauty. This design was selected to be exhibited at the 2017 New Designers exhibition which is where Jordan met the deVOL team.

Jordan began working at our main showroom in Cotes Mill for his training period, before joining the team at our Tysoe Street showroom in October 2017, where he takes customers' project ideas and inspirations and helps them to create their dream kitchen.

In his spare time, Jordan likes to keep active, going rock climbing and to concerts with his friends. To relax he enjoys taking trips to the cinema to see the latest films.

John achieved a First Class Honours degree from Buckingham Chilterns University College in 2005 and worked as a Kitchen Designer and Project Manager for Laings in Edinburgh until joining deVOL in 2010. It soon became clear that John's manufacturing knowledge and project management experience qualified him to not only design kitchens but to oversee the whole project through to completion.

For a project to run perfectly to plan requires a meticulous approach and an unflappable attitude. John has proven himself to be the perfect man for the job and customers are reassured by his obvious expertise and warm and friendly manner.

John enjoys helping his family out on occasion, making furniture and doing interior refurbishments, but mostly is happy going to the odd gig and having a night out with friends.

settings.staff_degree: BA (Hons) Interior Architecture and Venue Design
settings.staff_description:
Olivia graduated from the University of Derby in 2017 with a BA Honours in Interior Architecture & Venue Design, where she gained a thorough knowledge of the technical aspects to building as well as producing socially, culturally and environmentally responsive design proposals.

Whilst completing her degree, Olivia also attained her Diploma in Professional Practice and Project Management. Throughout her course, Olivia particularly enjoyed working with clients on current projects, including Urban Regeneration schemes which worked towards improving Derby and Nottingham city centres. During her final year, Olivia worked on the full architectural and interior renovation of Derby Assembly Rooms with Marketing Derby, where she used her creative flair and technical eye to create a design proposal that was not only innovative and practical, but also fully sustainable.

Now, Olivia loves managing our kitchen projects where she uses her knowledge and eye for detail to make sure every project runs smoothly from the sale to the installation and to deVOL’s extremely high standards. As a Project Manager, she liaises with our customers, Production team and Kitchen Designers on a daily basis to ensure our customers are happy throughout every step of the kitchen manufacture, delivery and installation process.

Olivia began travelling to places all over the world from a young age, experiencing the diverse cultures of Japan, India, Kefalonia, Belize, Costa Rica, Aruba, Jamaica and many more. Her plans for travel in the future include more exploration of countries closer to home such as the South of France, Switzerland and Sweden.

In her spare time, Olivia loves baking, antique shopping for her new home and keeping fit with a British Military Fitness group. She also has a passion for classic cars and enjoys driving her Nissan Figaro, with her Wire Haired Hungarian Vizsla, Worcester, as her passenger.

Alice graduated with a First Class Honours in Decorative Arts from Nottingham Trent University. Before joining the deVOL team as a Project Manager in the summer of 2019, she worked in fashion and textiles manufacture.

Overseeing the smooth running of deVOL projects all over the world is the main focus of Alice's role and after working at our Cotes Mill headquarters for a little while, she is now based at our Shepshed workshop where she is able to see the process of our furniture being made on a daily basis. Alice really enjoys working with the deVOL project management team and being so closely connected to the workshop. She also loves meeting and connecting with many different people during the whole kitchen design process and, of course, seeing the beautiful finished kitchens.

At the weekend, Alice enjoys cooking and taking her spaniels out for lovely long walks.

Abdul joined deVOL in 2020 after graduating from Loughborough University with a degree in Fine Art. During his studies, Abdul was particularly interested in notions of construction and deconstruction, and the way we consciously or unconsciously perceive art. Throughout his degree, Abdul experimented with video, sound, painting, collage, film and digital photography, sculpture, and print, and so we were very excited to see him apply this creativity to his work at deVOL.

As a Project Manager, Abdul is used to juggling several strict deadlines at once, all whilst helping our customers with any queries they might have about their project.

In his spare time, Abdul enjoys visiting the cinema or heading out on long walks across the UK. He’s also a keen sportsman, regularly playing football, basketball, tennis and badminton.

Charles joined the project management team at deVOL in 2019, where he is a key member of the staff offering technical support to our customers and making sure each project meets the level of excellence we expect.

Before coming to deVOL, Charles studied Product Design at Nottingham Trent University where he developed a strong interest in material process and properties. His degree project focussed on furniture, with the aim of reducing waste during a product lifecycle, and he was invited to display this work at the “New Designers” show.

Even when he’s not at work, Charles loves to take on small craft projects, particularly bladesmithing and metalwork.

Emily first started her training as a furniture maker at the young age of 15, working with a local company and learning the processes of design conception all the way to fitting new pieces in the home. Emily then went on to study at Rycotewood Furniture School, where she worked on several projects, focusing on minimalism and collaborating with Ercol, the Gordon Russell Museum, and the AHEC Foundation. She even took on some commission work for Oxford Council where she designed and made several of their museum cases.

In 2021, Emily joined our project management team, where she helps to ensure that each and every deVOL project runs smoothly and to our exacting standards.

Emily’s passion for furniture design spills into her life outside work, where she enjoys taking on furniture projects for her own home as well as collecting houseplants to go alongside them. When she’s not designing, Emily is a keen cook, and enjoys walking with friends and going camping.

Growing up in a family of builders, Jade has always had an interest in design and interiors. In 2020 she joined our team of Project Managers.

Working between our Leicestershire workshops, Jade takes your deVOL design and makes sure every step of the project runs as smoothly and easily as possible, right up to installation. Always at the end of the phone, Jade will be with you every step of the way to make sure your kitchen is exactly as you imagined!

When she’s not at work, Jade enjoys spending time with her family and Labrador, Lottie, as well as cooking delicious meals for her daughter, Marleigh.

After graduating from Loughborough University with a degree in Product Design Engineering, Katy joined deVOL as a Project Manager in January 2022.

This is a key role at deVOL and includes problem solving and offering technical support to our customers, as well as liaising with our designers and production team to ensure each and every kitchen is completed on time, and to our extremely high standards.

Katy is a keen painter and also describes herself as a big environmentalist, with a passion for nature and sustainability. She also likes to keep active by playing Ultimate Frisbee, and has received Duke of Edinburgh and Jack Petchey awards for her dedication to scouting.

Matt has a wealth of experience in many areas of kitchen design and manufacturing which made him a great addition to the deVOL team. He trained as a cabinet maker before undertaking a degree in Furniture Design, which focused on mass manufacturing techniques and design innovation. After graduating with a First Class Honours, he worked as a Project Manager and Designer for a number of years, producing designs and layouts for our clients and liaising with the workshop.

Before joining deVOL at the start of 2015 as a Kitchen Designer and Project Manager. Matt has a young family and loves to play a bit of squash when he gets the chance.

Emily joined deVOL in 2022 after graduating from Loughborough University with a First Class Honours in Graphic Design & Illustration. In the course of her studies, Emily had several of her illustrations exhibited at design shows across Leicester. She also studied film production, ceramics and graphic design at the University of Michigan and even worked on a short film that went to the Traverse Film Festival.

Here at deVOL, Emily works in our Project Management team, liaising with customers and designers to make sure every project runs smoothly with a beautiful final result. Emily particularly enjoys conducting site surveys, where she can meet customers in their homes and really help them visualise what their kitchen will look like.

Creative even outside of work, Emily spends much of her spare time illustrating greetings cards, posters and adult colouring books. When she’s not busy sketching, you can catch Emily cycling, visiting art galleries, and looking after her small family of houseplants.

Cameron joined deVOL in November 2024 as part of our brilliant project management team. Our Project Managers are a vital part of the deVOL design process, taking over from our kitchen designers once all the drawings are in place, and staying in touch with our customers right through until the very end of their project, when all the cupboards and accessories have been installed. Day-to-day, this means Cameron is responsible for liaising with our customers, answering any and every question they may have, as well as as finalising and verifying drawing details for our design and production teams.

When he’s not in work, you can still find Cameron working with furniture, crafting his own storage units as well as charcuterie and chopping boards. Cameron is passionate about sports and his weekends are full of watching or competing in all sorts of active endeavours.

After 8 years working in the motorcycle industry, Kat joined deVOL in December 2024, having been keen to pursue her interest in interiors and design.

As part of our project management team, Kat talks our customers through their final design and ensures every little detail is just right, so their kitchen installation goes smoothly. Kat is in touch with lots of different deVOL departments, from designers, to production, to logistics, ensuring everyone has all the information they need. You can also find Kat in our workshop, checking each drawer, door and cupboard meets our exacting standards, before they are sent out to our customers’ homes.

Kat is a big animal lover and a keen traveller, and spends her free time skiing and attending music festivals!

Molly joined us in October 2024 from Loughborough University, where she studied Textiles: Innovation and Design and specialised in print design and interiors. Molly’s final major project explored the history of the Shepshed Lace Company, inspired by her grandparent’s work there.

Molly now works in Shepshed herself, as part of deVOL's fantastic team of project managers. As a Project Manager, Molly oversees each element of our kitchen orders, right through from design completion to sign-off and installation, working closely with our lovely customers throughout.

In her free time, Molly enjoys going on walks, hanging out with her friends and baking sourdough bread!

Izzy graduated from Nottingham Trent University in July 2024, where she studied Interior Architecture and Design. This degree consisted of visiting many different sites, researching their history, creating concepts, designing spaces, making models and creating 3D visuals/renders for public spaces.

Joining deVOL in November 2024 to assist our project management team, Izzy was promoted to be a Project Manager herself in 2026. Izzy’s role involves completing site surveys at the very beginning of our design process and working with both our kitchen designers and customers to ensure the very final design looks beautiful and functions perfectly, too. Before any cupboards leave our workshops, Izzy will check each item to make sure it meets deVOL's exacting standards, and then liaise with our fitting team to ensure every piece is installed perfectly.

In her spare time, Izzy likes to read and go for walks with her Dachshund, Edie, and family. Izzy is also a passionate equestrian, having ridden horses since she was three years old and competed in dressage and show jumping.

Scarlett emigrated to Australia with her family when she was 17 where she lived for 5 and a half years. Whilst living in Australia she completed a Bachelor of Media at the University of Adelaide. Scarlett took the opportunity to explore the vast country whilst living down under and visited Sydney, Melbourne, Ayers Rock and The Great Barrier Reef. Upon returning to the UK, Scarlett studied for an MSc in Applied Equine Science from Writtle College Essex whilst working as a horse groom.

Shortly after completing her MSc, Scarlett joined the deVOL team in June 2015 at our Cotes Mill showrooms. Scarlett's friendly, helpful and smiley manner makes her the perfect person to work on our reception desk, greeting all of the lovely customers that visit us each day and making them feel welcome. Scarlett's hard work and dedication saw he promoted to showroom manager in October 2018 where she continues to keep everything running smoothly.

Scarlett also deals with all deVOL Accessories purchases, she liaises with customers to take their orders, arrange delivery and ensure this process is smooth and enjoyable. This can be orders for anything from our popular Aged Brass taps, Handcrafted Knobs and Handles, our beautiful Hanging Rails and Hooks, right down to oak Chopping Boards and Laundry Maids from the Wooden Accessories range that we launched many years ago.

Another of Scarlett's roles at deVOL is organising, pricing up and displaying all of the deliveries of beautiful new stock, the lovely and unique extras that are intermingled and for sale around the Cotes Mill showrooms. Gifts, cards, books, stationery, unusual things for your home and garden, and of course a selection of fabulous vintage and antique pieces that we source from all over the world.

In her spare time, Scarlett loves spending time with her horses, Archie and Pogo, as well as seeing her friends and family and going on holidays!

Georgina graduated from Nottingham Trent University in 2011 with a 2:1 in Photography. Her final project went on to win two awards and inspired her to create two books and stage her own solo exhibition.

Georgina joined deVOL in 2019 as a Showroom Assistant and was quickly promoted to Assistant Showroom Manager in 2020. Her day-to-day tasks involve welcoming customers to our lovely Cotes Mill showroom as well as assisting with customer enquiries and orders. Georgina's favourite part of her role is helping to create inspiring displays, using her visual experience to make sure our showroom is reflecting deVOL's creative vision at all times. Georgina loves seeing how our Creative Director, Helen, works first-hand.

In her spare time, Georgina enjoys spending time with her family, taking beautiful photographs, spending time camping in nature and learning new creative skills.

Joining the deVOL team in July 2023, Liberty is based at our historic Cotes Mill headquarters in Leicestershire. As our Assistant Customer Advisor, she is often the very first point of call for customers requiring help and advice with their online shop orders. Day to day, you'll find Liberty answering queries, advising on product specs and ensuring everybody has a happy and easy shopping experience with deVOL.

Liberty is a trained professional dancer and before joining deVOL, she spent five years working within the production show cast for Princess Cruises, travelling the world and interacting with guests from a vast variety of different countries and cultures.

As a qualified yoga teacher, Liberty regularly runs yoga workshops. In her spare time, she enjoys being outside and riding her horse, Toby, in the beautiful countryside.

Chloe started at deVOL in April 2025, joining the showroom team at our inspiring Cotes Mill headquarters. A busy day may see Chloe answering customer emails and phone calls, welcoming visitors to the showroom, advising on the extensive range of home accessories that we offer, ensuring the kitchen displays are tidy and looking beautiful, and lending a hand to anyone that needs it! All this expertise is put to work in her own home, where she’s planning several large renovation projects.

Outside of deVOL, Chloe is a student at the Open University, studying towards her Business Management degree, and you can frequently find her on the netball court, having played for the last 10 years. Further afield, Chloe enjoys travelling, with recent trips including swimming in the Great Barrier Reef and volunteering in Costa Rica.

After completing a degree in Political Science at the University of York, Rhys went on to be a manager at a local chain of pubs. Following this, he worked at a local gin company as a distiller before moving on to looking after UK sales & brand management there. 

Rhys joined deVOL in 2019 as our Customer Service Manager at the Cotes Mill headquarters. This very important role sees Rhys looks after all aspects of the customer experience, from giving tours around our beautiful showroom and grounds, to helping people popping in to look at our eclectic range of gifts and vintage furniture, right through to those who are having a full deVOL Kitchen fitted. As the general point of contact at Cotes Mill, Rhys will do his very best to help you out or point you in the direction of the best person for your query, ensuring you have an easy and enjoyable experience with deVOL. 

Cozy pubs, cool bars and big meals out are some of Rhys' favourite things, and he also makes a great cup of tea, so if you ever do visit us at Cotes Mill, look for Rhys! One day, he would love to own his house and maybe even have a deVOL Kitchen!

George joined deVOL in 2010 on a one year placement and returned as a permanent member of staff after completing his degree in Industrial Design and Technology at Loughborough University with a First Class Honours degree.

During his placement year George held various responsibilities including being part of the design team, managing dispatches and dealing with orders for accessories. Since returning to the company full time, his role has developed and he now manages the everyday production at our workshops on Jubilee Drive and at The Locks.

It is George’s responsibility to ensure that the manufacture of every deVOL Kitchen runs as smoothly as possible. He maintains a strong link between Project Managers, the production team and all of the workshops to ensure that everyone has the information they require to complete each stage of manufacture. Working closely with our Workshop Managers, George puts quality control checks in place; these ensure all of our furniture passes through each process at deVOL’s impossibly high standards with no exceptions. George also helps to develop new processes and improve the production methods already in place to push the company forward.

The problem solving aspects of George’s job is something he particularly enjoys and knowing just how much effort is put into every single deVOL cupboard means he takes a lot of pride in the furniture we design and make.

George has always had a keen interest in furniture and wood due to his Grandad, who made a career in carpentry. He has always enjoyed constructing his own pieces of furniture and during his final year at University George designed and made a plywood bicycle for children that had an adjustable frame to allow it to be raised as the child grows.

In his spare time George enjoys a wide range of sports including cycling, running and skiing. Since buying his first house he has taken on many new projects and spends most weekends decorating or building things to fill it with.

Alex studied Genetics at Manchester University. For his final year project, he studied the development of fish circulatory systems. Alex oversees the operation of our CNC machines, during his studies he designed and constructed laboratory equipment rigs.

Before working supervising deVOL’s CNC department, Alex spent time working in our Shaker kitchen workshop, learning the production processes of our kitchens and then working as part of the production team. This also allowed Alex to develop an understanding of the workings of the warehouse and the dispatch system for kitchens.

Alex is an avid rugby fan and regularly plays for for Loughborough Rugby Club 2nd team. He also enjoys watching American football, which he played throughout his time at university, and has recently taken up archery and scuba diving.

Dominic joined the production team at deVOL after graduating from Birmingham Institute of Art and Design in 2014 with a 2:1. He spent a few months in the workshop building up his carpentry and joinery skills which helped develop an understanding of the company and its processes. Dominic then joined the production team where he now produces cutting lists for bespoke furniture and helps with the general day to day workings of the office and workshop to keep things running smoothly.

Dominic is a very practical and creative individual and is always working on one creative project or another, anything from making picture books, animations and even a life sized mdf yeti. His passion for woodwork stems from his grandad who was building currachs (fishing boats) for local fisherman up into his mid 90's.

Adam joined the deVOL team in 2015 after graduating from the University of Derby with a 2:1 in Product Design, focusing on furniture and industrial design with a particular interest in woodwork and prototype modelling.

Although Adam initially joined as a Project Manager, his impressive eye for detail and a keen interest in technical drawings and manufacture soon saw him move to our production team where he produced drawings and cutting lists for our Shaker kitchens and wooden worktops as well as working on some aspects of our bespoke Classic English range. It wasn't long before Adam began training new employees and took on the responsibility of managing the production of all Sebastian Cox projects.
