In this role, he played a significant part in streamlining production, allowing for growth and improving efficiency.

Adam became Production Manager in 2022 and now oversees deVOL's production, managing the team and our kitchen projects from the design through to dispatch, with a main focus on our Sebastian Cox and Shaker ranges.

In his spare time, Adam enjoys doing arts and crafts with his children as well as hand-making candles and soaps. You'll regularly find him at the gym or the pool or going on long walks with friends and family and his Border Collie Cross, Bella.

Upon finishing his A levels Ben went to work for Caterpillar Building Construction Products in Leicester on a year's placement where, as a Manufacturing Engineer, he was responsible for designing and prototyping tooling and jigs for use on the production lines. Ben then went on to study Architecture at the University of Plymouth, graduating in 2011, with particular interests in vernacular architecture, materiality and the use of emergent design systems.

Whilst studying, Ben also took part in several student workshops and led a design and build project in which a team of students created outdoor showering facilities from locally grown bamboo and reclaimed wood.

After graduating Ben spent several months working and travelling in Europe, first building yurts and a round-wood timber framed roundhouse for use as holiday accommodation in the Dordogne, and then on a large scale restoration project turning an old stone farmhouse into accommodation and teaching spaces for an arts retreat in Italy.

Ben's interests include cycling, photography and greenwood carpentry and he has recently completed a willow weaving course, learning to make hurdles and salmon traps.

Pete studied Furniture and Product Design at Nottingham Trent University before moving to Devon to study and work alongside some of the UK's best bespoke furniture makers. Whilst in Devon, Pete learnt the intricacies of furniture making, from the raw timber to the finished piece, all created by hand. 

After running a small bespoke furniture business for a while, hand-making pieces for clients, Pete went on to help out local art and design galleries with installations. Pete utilised CNC technology and married it with hand-finishing methods to produce elegant solutions for his clients' needs, some of which Pete took to Designjunction in 2015 to exhibit and sell. 

Now at deVOL, Pete's love for designing and making with real wood is coupled with his love for one-on-one client-based customer service. Pete enjoys getting to know the customer to fully understand what each individual project needs. 

Out of hours, Pete loves to play the drums and has been lucky enough to tour around the world playing shows with friends and some more well-known artists. This has provided him with amazing opportunities to live in New York and Los Angeles and see many other countries, which have inspired his creativity and passion for design.

Josh joined deVOL in 2017 as a Production Assistant after graduating from Sheffield Hallam where he received a CHE in Furniture Design.

After completing his degree, Josh went on to work in the design and manufacture of student accommodation. In this role he was administering projects in the UK and Ireland, producing cost plans, manufacturing orders and designing bespoke pieces which required attending site for meetings and fitting progress reports. He also took part in a couple of short courses in Architectural Modelling and CAD at Nottingham Trent University.

During his spare time Josh enjoys restoring classic cars, is currently working on a few wood and metal projects, and enjoys going clay pigeon shooting.

Sam graduated from Bucks New University in 2014 where he had studied Furniture: Contemporary Design. Sam has always had passions for woodworking and technology so during his time at University he particularly enjoyed experimenting with CAD software and CNC machines as well as developing skills in fine cabinet making. He has since showcased ranges of furniture at both the New Designers exhibition and the May Design Series.

Based in our office at Cotes Mill Sam works as part of the production team creating both CNC programs and technical drawings for the workshop to make our designs into reality. During his time at deVOL Sam has used his extensive material knowledge to get involved in the manufacture of all kitchen ranges and furniture.

Outside of furniture & woodwork Sam enjoys getting into a project and getting his hands dirty especially if there is an engine involved. He has a passion for old vehicles and motorcycles and frequently attends events all over the country with like-minded individuals.

After spending three seasons working as a ski technician in Les Deux Alpes and running his own catering business in the Isle of Man, Tom joined deVOL in August 2005 to assist with the development of deVOL's new offices. Tom is such a warm and supportive character and after a few years of training and making furniture at deVOL he became the natural choice for new apprentices to turn to for help.

Tom was promoted to Assistant Workshop Manager in 2008 and then to Workshop Manager when deVOL opened it's second workshop.

Tom is a keen snowboarder, blues guitarist and vocalist. Since joining deVOL Tom has become a proud father of two lovely daughters.

Ryan has ten years of experience in the woodworking and manufacturing industry and is a very highly motivated member of our team who is always pushing himself and the workshop he manages. Ryan has an exceptionally broad range of skills that equip him to tackle any job and he is instrumental in the continuing development of deVOL’s Real Shaker range of furniture.

In his spare time, Ryan enjoys playing rugby and is a talented golfer with an impressive handicap.

Ryan has just completed the renovation of his house and is now undertaking the construction of an extension, of which he will carry out a large portion of the work. There seems to be nothing that Ryan will not take on and excel at.

Gavin joined deVOL in 2015 following a long career in retail. As a trained Guitar Luthier, Gavin has considerable knowledge of woodworking and this, combined with his exemplary work ethic, saw him promoted to head of the Fascias Department in 2017. Gavin’s role now involves overseeing the ordering of timber and all processes leading up to our beautiful kitchen furniture heading off to be painted. Outside of deVOL, Gavin is a keen cinephile, collecting original movie posters and memorabilia. On the weekends you can find him visiting film conventions or travelling to locations from his favourite scenes, to document 'then & now' comparisons for his Instagram page.

Gemma completed a National Diploma in Healthcare at Stephensons College in Leicestershire, before pursuing her passion for food and working as a chef for four years. Gemma loves everything to do with food, from cooking to baking to eating out, and always picks her holiday destinations based on the cuisine! 

After a slight career change, Gemma joined deVOL to help hand-paint all of our beautiful furniture and quickly proved herself to be an extremely skilled and hard-working member of the team, now working as deVOL’s Workshop Manager.

Gemma will always have a love for hand-painting and still gets to use her skills from time to time, going on site to customers’ homes to complete any painting remedial work, from a full repaint to the last little finishing touches.  

When she’s not in the spray shop, Gemma has also been polishing and ageing all of deVOL’s gorgeous mottled copper worktops. Her wide skill set and amazing work ethic make Gemma a highly valued member of the deVOL team. 

In her spare time, Gemma loves to read, particularly Shakespeare and books based on true historical events, such as the Second World War. She also loves spending time with her husband and dog after a long day at work!

Justin has always had a keen interest in DIY after spending lots of time learning from and working with his father, who shares his love for carpentry. After leaving college he spent 9 years working and gaining experience within the family business, making UPVC windows, doors and conservatories.

In 2014 Justin joined deVOL as a bench joiner and after showing great skill and utter determination to create furniture of the absolute best quality, he was given the position of Assistant Workshop Manager.

Justin continued to show his skill and great attention to detail and was promoted to Workshop Manager in early 2016. Now in charge of our Real Shaker Kitchen production, Justin ensures every single kitchen that leaves our Loughborough workshop is made on time and to deVOL’s impossibly high standards.

A year and a half ago Justin took on the challenge of buying his first home and renovating it single-handedly from top to bottom; a very testing and demanding project, but so worth it in the end. Justin loves getting stuck into these types of projects and is always thinking of what he can put his hand to next.

In his late teens Justin played semi professional football and although he’s no longer playing, he still enjoys keeping fit by running, regularly going to the gym and walking his dog. Travelling is another of Justin’s passions; he’s been on trips to Asia and America and also loves visiting the Lake District for a piece of the good old English countryside!

Kyle joined deVOL as a Finishing Shop Assistant in 2015. Before joining the team in our Loughborough workshop, he previously worked two jobs as a Decorative Glass Manufacturer and at Aldi as a Night Stock Assistant. The decorative glass company also owned a mechanical rodeo bull and surf simulator business, which Kyle assisted with during quieter periods and thoroughly enjoyed.

Whilst working for these companies, Kyle took real pride in his jobs which required lots of attention to detail. An interest for DIY and wood working projects lead Kyle to join deVOL. Remaining enthusiastic at work allows Kyle to do the best possible job and ensure every piece of furniture is finished to deVOL's very high standards. Kyle's dedication and passion for work made him a great addition to our team and lead him to become a Workshop Manager. 

In his spare time, Kyle enjoys playing the guitar and going for long country walks and is currently learning to snowboard too. Having recently become a father, Kyle is enjoying family life and he amazing experiences this brings.

Tom studied and completed Level 2 NVQ in carpentry and joinery, as well as a Level 2 NVQ in maintenance. Throughout his studies, Tom worked as a baker at Morrisons, before starting his first full time job on a site.

He worked on site for a few years, working from the ground up, digging trenches, building walls, hanging doors and putting roofs on were all skills he gained whilst working there.

Since joining deVOL as a bench joiner in 2015, Tom has thoroughly enjoyed his new role. He developed quickly with a positive approach and a hunger to learn, which led to Tom becoming the Workshop Manager. He's enjoying managing his team and seeing the beautifully finished products go out to customers all over the country.

Tom is a family man with a young daughter, Olivia. In his spare time he enjoys watching sports and has a competitive streak when it comes to a game of table tennis!

After working as a hair stylist in London's West End for 15 years, Henry decided to retire his scissors and join the deVOL team as a joiner in 2020. Now the Assistant Manager of our Sebastian Cox department, Henry can be found crafting freestanding furniture and wall cupboards and using his keen eye for detail to make sure every single item is completed to deVOL’s exacting requirements.

Outside of work, Henry loves to ski and swim outdoors and in 2017 he raised £20k for charity, swimming for 14 hours attempting to cross the English Channel. Ever the joiner, Henry spends his free time repairing bats for his local cricket team, which he also plays for, and hopes to make one of his own soon!

Reece joined deVOL in 2016 after completing his Level 1 Bench Joinery and Level 2 Site Carpentry Diploma at Leicester College.

Having worked across many areas of deVOL, starting as a fascia maker, Reece was instrumental in helping to create a highly productive door-making department. Since then, Reece has become one of our workshop managers, running both door manufacturing and the machine shop and helping to ensure every single part of every single cupboard is made to the incredibly high requirements that we demand at deVOL.

Outside of work, Reece is a father to two amazing little boys, Wilfred and Otto, and in his spare time he enjoys going to the pub with friends, gigs and gaming. Reece also loves to travel and some of his favourite destinations have included New York, Thailand, Vietnam and Bali but the bucket list is ever-growing!

Duncan joined deVOL in 2019 as a bench joiner and quickly worked his way up to become the manager of our fascia department. Day-to-day, Duncan oversees the smooth running of the workshop making our Shaker and Classic English fascias. A real deVOL expert, Duncan is always on hand to assist our other workshop departments and ensure that every piece of cabinetry is made to our incredibly high standards.

Before joining deVOL, Duncan studied Sports Management at Bournemouth University, and even spent a year coaching soccer in Boston, USA. In his free time, you can find Duncan enjoying various sports, as well as walking his two dogs.

settings.staff_degree: BA (Hons) Fine Art & MA Fine Art & Design Studio Practices
settings.staff_description:
Lewis joined deVOL in 2012 after receiving his BA Hons in Fine Art and an MA in Fine Art & Design Studio Practices. Still a part-time artist, Lewis has used his artworks to raise money for children’s charities since graduating in 2010 and has even displayed his pieces at Mansion House in London for the Lord Mayor and Lady Mayoress.

Here at deVOL, Lewis manages the hard-working team responsible for making our Classic English kitchens. Lewis particularly enjoys focussing on ways to make the range more efficient without sacrificing the integral high quality of each piece of furniture.

In his free time, Lewis is a bit of a foodie and a big traveller. Catch him free diving in Thailand or climbing a volcano in Guatemala or just chilling on a beach.

Having achieved a BA Hons in Photography and Video at De Montfort University, James spent the next few years working and travelling across Finland, France and Cornwall. Spurred on by the enjoyment he got from renovating his first house, James decided to make a career change in 2017, and joined deVOL as a Bench Joiner.

James started out in our Shaker department, honing his skills building our freestanding furniture. Nowadays, James manages the incredibly talented team who construct deVOL's Haberdasher’s Kitchen, our most technical range of cabinetry.

In his spare time, James enjoys being in the outdoors, mountain biking, walking his two dogs, and spending time with his son.

Adrian came to the UK in 1999 after several years living and working across the US, Hong Kong and Macau, gaining experience in lots of different roles. Having already spent some time working in kitchen design, Adrian joined the deVOL team in 2018.

Starting as a Dispatch Assistant, Adrian became our Workshop Dispatch Manager in 2021. Adrian coordinates with many different deVOL departments to make sure that all our UK and international deliveries run smoothly so customers can get their beautiful new kitchens without any delays.

In his spare time, Adrian enjoys reading history and spending time with his family. He also finds time to play rugby at Loughborough RFC and enjoys watching his daughters play too.

Neil has been passionate about woodwork and has wanted to pursue this career since he was a teenager, completing an NVQ Level 3 in carpentry before joining the deVOL team in 2015.

Having worked in both our Despatch and Shaker Assembly departments over the past 8 years, Neil is a real expert in all aspects of deVOL furniture, and was promoted to Assistant Manager of our Shaker workshop in 2022. This role requires Neil to make sure that every single Shaker cupboard is made and finished to the incredibly high standard that we require of all our designs.

Outside of work, Neil enjoys spending his weekends walking his Red Fox Labrador, Ruben, or jetting off on holiday to ski or explore Caribbean islands.

Dale joined deVOL in 2018 as a Trainee Bench Joiner working on the Shaker range, with his main role being to assemble the final cabinets ready to be sent out to our lovely customers' homes.

Having mastered our Shaker furniture, Dale moved to our Classic English department, where he perfected hand finishing and assembling deVOL's bespoke kitchens. Before long, Dale was promoted to Assistant Workshop Manager, helping to ensure the smooth running of this busy department.

In his free time, Dale enjoys cooking, especially barbecuing, seeking out new recipes and even creating a few of his own! When he’s not cooking up a storm, Dale is busy with his family, heading out on his bike or going for walks.

Ellie graduated from De Montfort University with a First Class degree in Design Crafts, specialising in mould-making and slipcasting. For her final collection, she created a range of tableware and lighting, drawing inspiration from the juxtaposition between Brutalist architecture and traditional Japanese calligraphy. Her work was chosen to exhibit at New Designers, one of the UK’s biggest events for emerging talent, and she was also awarded the Albert Thomas Roberts Art & Crafts Scholarship Award at her degree show.

Ellie joined our growing ceramics department in the summer of 2019 and quickly became a key member of the team, assisting with all aspects of production. In 2021, Ellie became the Ceramics Studio Assistant Manager. Her main role is to ensure the smooth running of the studio and to continue to improve our processes.

Outside of work, Ellie spends time in her home studio, where she has her own kiln. She runs pottery workshops and takes part in many craft fairs selling tableware, homeware and jewellery. Ellie’s work is also stocked in a few local shops and has even been featured in Country Living Modern Rustic magazine. When she’s not at the wheel, Ellie can be found spending time with her family and young daughter, Everly.

Jim studied Fine Art at Kingston University, graduating with a First Class degree in 2015. He was subsequently awarded London Bronze Foundry's 'Ingot' prize with his collaborator before working for multiple art galleries in technical capacities including sculpture fabrication, gallery installation, performance and sound design.

Jim joined deVOL in 2018, working within the ceramics department for a year before travelling and working for a bronze sculpture foundry in Sydney, Australia. Returning to deVOL in 2020, Jim's role within the ceramics department is now primarily focused on developing and streamlining our production processes. He can often be found devising new equipment, adjusting glazes and working out new ways to utilise our trusty kilns.

Outside of work, Jim maintains a studio practice that includes printmaking, ceramics and drawing. Jim is also a musician, regularly playing live in his bands and as a solo performer.

Sophie joined deVOL in July 2022 after graduating from De Montfort University with a 2:1 in Design Crafts. Her final project was a curiosity collection of thrown ceramic jars, inspired by the fine details, patterns and textures found in Victorian Gothic architecture. For this collection, she was awarded ‘Ceramics and Glass Designer of the Year’ at New Designers 2022.

Day to day, Sophie assists and oversees ceramic production, particularly our porcelain lighting and emerald green tiles. She is also keen to lend her hand to creative problem solving and developing new products.

Outside of work, you can find Sophie at a show, whether this be live music, a food festival, a theatre trip or a drag performance.

Jade joined deVOL in 2023 after achieving a First Class Degree in Fine Art at Nottingham Trent University. Her final project was a collection of large vases featuring intricate 3D designs inspired by her time in South Korea, where she studied East Asian Art History at Yonsei University.

At deVOL, Jade is our Ceramics Production Supervisor and a vital part of the team responsible for creating the ceramic designs for which deVOL has become so well known. She particularly focuses on our unique Lace Market Tiles and also helps to develop new glazes and expand our range of ceramic offerings.

When she’s not in the ceramics studio, Jade enjoys spending time with her three greyhounds, Banana, Pecan and Pickle, as well as playing computer games and cooking.

Stephanie joined deVOL in October 2016 after achieving a First Class Honours in Jewellery and Accessories at Middlesex University, London.

During her time at university, she experimented with combining a wide range of materials and techniques. Mainly influenced by London architecture and scaffolding, Stephanie’s graduate collection ‘Fragments’ was inspired by geometric structures, industrial materials and minimalistic design. After exhibiting her collection at New Designers, Stephanie was invited to show her work across the UK in galleries such as Gill Wing in London, Kath Libbert in Saltaire and Lustre in Nottingham. Stephanie’s work was also selected amongst the top international jewellery graduates to show at Galerie Marzee in the Netherlands, the largest jewellery gallery in the world! Since then she has continued to show internationally and is soon exhibiting at Amsterdam and Munich Jewellery Week.

Stephanie now spends her days at Cotes Mill in her new metals studio, fettling, casting and hammering away at metal. Everyone has watched in awe as Stephanie showed us the basics of jewellery making, restored our amazing antique chandelier for the new London showroom, created the fixtures for our lovely new ceramic pendants and took on the task of making a brand new range of beautiful handmade door furniture for deVOL. Check out a video of Stephanie making our beautiful new brass cup handles.

Having grown up in North Wales, on the stunningly picturesque Isle of Anglesey, Stephanie enjoys a wide range of outdoor activities and exploring Snowdonia National Park. In her spare time you’ll find her making jewellery in her studio, at the local climbing wall or travelling back to Wales to see her family.

Zoë joined the deVOL team in 2012 after completing her A-Levels at Loughborough College where she studied English Literature, Art and Photography.

After working at deVOL’s beautiful Loughborough showrooms for a couple of years, Zoë’s dream of moving to London came true when we opened up our lovely little Tysoe St. shop in Clerkenwell.

Now working from the London showroom, Zoë manages all of deVOL's PR and marketing with the help of our PR and Marketing assistant, Letty. They gain deVOL great exposure in all of the top magazines and on the best blogs across the world. Zoë’s jobs include writing, designing and sending out press releases on our latest kitchens, products and news to journalists and bloggers, regularly contributing to the deVOL Journal and responding to the many editorial image requests we receive on a daily basis.

Managing all of deVOL’s social media platforms is one of Zoë’s favourite parts of her job, starting all of the accounts with zero followers, to seeing them grow to tens of thousands of followers is amazing. Interacting on a daily basis with customers, industry professionals and people who just love what deVOL do is such a cool part of her job.

Zoë is also responsible for booking, creating and sending off all of deVOL’s national and local adverts, reviewing our advertising offers and chatting with new magazines and journals to see if they’d be the perfect fit for deVOL.

In her spare time, Zoë likes to go out with her friends, go to gigs and festivals and help Letty tick things off her forever expanding London bucket list! Zoë also loves to travel, with recent trips to Berlin, Budapest, Amsterdam and Paris, next on her list is LA and New York!

Holly graduated from the University of Nottingham with First Class Honours in English Literature and Language in 2017. She has always wanted to work in PR and has a keen interest in interior design, so joining the little PR & Marketing team at deVOL in 2018 was perfect.

Holly works with Zoë, Letty and Lydia, helping to manage the social media platforms, dealing with editorial requests, helping with press releases, writing content for the deVOL Journal and much more. She loves every aspect of her job, from watching the social media following continue to grow, to seeing deVOL's latest projects in the top magazines and on the best blogs.

In September 2019, Holly made the move to New York! She loves working in our beautiful Bond Street showroom and is having the best time exploring this incredible city and the rest of the States.

settings.staff_degree: BSc (Hons) Human Geography & MSc Development Studies
settings.staff_description:
Lydia graduated from the University of Exeter with a First Class Honours in Human Geography and then went on to study for her Master's in Development Studies at SOAS University of London, gaining a Merit. Looking to move away from academia into a more creative field, Lydia joined deVOL's PR and Marketing team in December 2020, working from the beautiful St. John's Square showroom. 

Having worked in social media previously, Lydia really enjoys creating engaging content for deVOL's Instagram and Twitter feeds, writing for the deVOL Journal and connecting with our customers online. She also helps the team to keep on top of all editorial features and contributes to the quarterly deVOL newsletter.

Outside of work, Lydia loves to travel. Recent trips have included visits to Malaysia, Singapore and Ghana, next up it's Japan! Closer to home she enjoys hunting down French bakeries, playing the piano, and spending time with friends.

Tim Graduated with a 2:1 from Lincoln University in May 2007 and joined deVOL that June. Tim's portfolio of work showed varied interests, social documentary and experimental film photography as well as stunt BMX videos taken during trips to Spain and Texas.

Tim has stayed with deVOL since graduating, photographing beautiful kitchens at our studios, showrooms and on location at our client's houses. His photos have appeared in numerous national and international interior magazines and newspapers including Elle Decoration, House & Garden, The World of Interiors and The Sunday Times. As well as Tim’s photos appearing in some of the best magazines in the world, they have also appeared on some of the top and most well respected design and interiors blogs such as Remodelista, Apartment Therapy and Dezeen.

Tim has also taken nearly all the photographs and videos for our other companies, with work ranging from filming our underwear model striding around a Nottingham shopping centre in his pants to the incredibly detailed photos of natural stone floor tiles that show every subtle difference in hue and texture.

Working closely with our Creative Director, Helen Parker, Tim has taken some of the highest quality interior and still life product photos we have ever produced; photographs which finally do our products justice. Our beautiful photography is what sells our kitchens, it’s so important to us to get every photo just right, whether it’s for our social media pages or a full page national advert. Tim has worked incredibly hard to perfect his art and his photos just keep getting better with every shoot.

Working with an in-house photographer on a daily basis seems to be the only way to achieve such stunning results. Tim's dedication and versatility has earned him the position of Design Office Manager and he now oversees the work of our other graphic and web designers as well as helping with our IT support, on-going SEO and kitchen brochure design and printing.

One of Tim’s favourite shoots was of our Classic English Clapham Kitchen, the cupboards were stunning and so substantial, they really did feel like they’d last a lifetime and it was a space you just wanted to spend time in. The Arts and Crafts Kitchen photoshoot is another highlight for Tim, with tall vaulted ceilings, huge windows and beautifully soft light; it was a photographer’s dream.

Most recently, Tim has been working on a series of beautifully shot short films to show the making process of some of deVOL’s newest products, including our handmade ceramic tiles, kitchenware collection and our brand new aged brass cup handles, some of which have been viewed over thirty thousand times each on our social media pages.

Tim has just finished a complete home renovation, gutting the whole house from top to bottom and starting from scratch. He even laid a parquet floor by hand over the whole ground floor, a long and meticulous task but so worth it in the end.

In his spare time, Tim is a very keen cyclist and has cycled in the French Alps and Pyrenees. He likes walking and landscape photography, particularly in the peak district, working on his garden and hanging out with his cats, Barney and Betty. Exploring European cities is another of Tim’s loves, with his favourites so far being Berlin and Barcelona.

Huw joined deVOL in November 2015 after graduating from Loughborough University with a First Class Honours in Fine Art. His education and many different creative hobbies have allowed him to develop a keen eye for design.

Huw has quickly worked his way up to become Creative Design Manager and is a key member of the team, overseeing all of deVOL’s graphic design work and putting his enviable patience and amazing teaching skills to work when training and helping new members of our graphics team.

It’s crazy how much stuff Huw knows, he is great at maths and is an absolute fountain of knowledge; we no longer use Google in the office, we now use ‘Huwgle’! Huw excels at anything he puts his mind to, he’s just really good at everything and is a true asset to deVOL.

Recently, Huw has been heavily involved in a lot of deVOL’s product and furniture design projects. Using 3D modelling software, he designed and created the curved seat pan for our beautiful new Bum Stool, the comfiest solid oak stool you will ever sit on.

Huw has been helping our jeweller, Stephanie, model and 3D print the master patterns of her cup handle designs to be used in the sand casting process for our range of beautiful brass door furniture. He has also been working on lots of other projects that we have in the works, including new lighting products, a deVOL table and chair and our vintage VW camper van, which we hope to transform into the deVOL food truck.

Proving that Huw really can do anything, late last year he travelled down to our lovely new London showroom and townhouse to hand-paint the deVOL logo above the showroom door. We watched in awe as he kept an impossibly steady hand and painted every little detail, every shadow and every highlight just spot on.

In his spare time, Huw remains a practising visual artist and musician; he designs and produces intricate geometric colour compositions, each responding to a specific piece of music. These designs have been executed as paintings, mosaics, digital images, prints and large-scale kinetic installations. Shortly after graduating, Huw’s work was shortlisted for a number of national and local graduate prizes – winning the runner-up prize for the LSA Student Award 2015.

Huw has a highly active presence in his local music community. Since 2010, he has been regularly recording and performing around the country in a hillbilly-style blues band called The Anteloids; playing drums, washboard and the saxophone. He is also one of the organisers for The Pig Applestock Festival; a local charity music festival held at Naseby reservoir in August. All of the funds raised by the festival are donated to the MS Therapy Centre in Leicestershire.

Millie joined deVOL in the summer of 2021, with a big passion for graphic design, interior design and all things creative, as well as three years of experience working in a marketing and graphic design role, and two years within the design team at a furniture manufacturer.

Growing up in a busy household, surrounded by makers and craftspeople, Millie is very familiar with the smell of sawdust, the sound of tools and the sight of people crafting the most beautiful things from wood, which is what makes her feel so at home here at deVOL.

Within the Creative Design team, Millie produces artwork for advertising, creates branded materials, assists with keeping the website up to date, and helps out with lots of other exciting projects too.

Millie's keen interest in design has led her through various courses and classes, including a Foundation Diploma in Art & Design and a Diploma in Graphic Design, as well as taking part in short courses to learn new creative skills.

At the weekend, Millie likes wandering around antique shops looking for treasures for her home and spending lots of time outdoors, walking with her dog, running or biking, just as long as there is a coffee shop on route!

Farhan joined deVOL in September 2023 following his degree in Graphic Design at Sheffield Hallam University. During his studies, Farhan worked as a fashion photographer, and his images were used on Malaysian national TV, as well as a few local fashion magazines.

Here at deVOL, Farhan has a varied role supporting the Creative Design team in the many exciting projects they do. As a Graphic Designer, Farhan works from our beautiful Cotes Mill showroom, and can be found editing images from our latest photoshoots, creating mockups for our website, and designing beautiful postcards for the deVOL showrooms.

Outside of work, Farhan remains passionate about photography and enjoys the process of editing and creating the perfect shot. Farhan also has an interest in travel and humanitarian work. Whilst at university Farhan visited Kathmandu, Nepal, where he helped to install a water filter pump for several local villages. An avid gamer, Farhan enjoys esports but also appreciates a quiet moment reading.

Kishan graduated from the University of Westminster in 2020 with a DipHE in Computer Science. Joining deVOL in 2023, Kishan put his considerable expertise in SEO and Google Analytics to work immediately, helping to make it as easy as possible for people to find deVOL online. In addition to this, Kishan helps to manage the deVOL website, making style edits, and ensuring our stock management systems are running smoothly and effectively.

When he’s not at work, Kishan plays tennis for Charnwood Lawn Tennis Club, but he’s a keen musician, posting English and Hindi guitar and singing videos on social media, and he’s now learning to play the Bansuri flute! Kishan also loves to travel and aims to visit 100 countries, 35 down 65 to go...

Alysha graduated in 2016 with a Masters in Aerospace Engineering from Sheffield Hallam University. For the next six years, Alysha worked as a Technical Sales Consultant in the software industry, but felt she needed to do something more creative, so retrained as a web developer. Alysha then spent a year learning languages like HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python and React JS, alongside some frameworks such as Bootstrap and Django (drf).

Fulfilling her ambition to enter a more creative field, Alysha joined deVOL in September 2024 as a Web Developer in our Creative Design team. Her responsibilities now include producing new features on the website for product launches or content pages, maintaining and adjusting the styling on the frontend to improve UI, and supporting back end processes and systems, such as order management and dispatch.

Outside of work, you’ll usually find Alysha with her nose in a book or in the middle of a crochet project. Alysha has also been tap dancing for 4 years and takes part in a yearly charity dance for Children In Need to try and break the world record for the number of people tap dancing to the same song at the same time!

settings.staff_description:
Ben qualified with distinction from Hereford Technical College as a cabinet maker in 1989 and worked for Paul Somers Interiors and Woodgate Woodcraft Ltd gaining valuable knowledge from experienced craftsmen.

Ben returned to college in 1992, and excelled in successive courses, namely: a BTEC in Art Design, a HND in Textiles and finally a First Class honours degree in Multimedia. Ben's college work was selected for 100% Design and the New Designers exhibition where he won the prestigious 1997 Design Guild Award. Ben's chubby carpet scooter sculptures and other imaginative works have been exhibited in London's Mall Gallery, as well as Durham, Berlin and The Maze Gallery, Turin.

Following his graduation, Ben worked for a year designing, making and fitting boat interiors before joining deVOL in 1998 as one of our cabinet makers. After 3 years Ben proved his passion, skill and determination to create beautiful furniture of the absolute highest quality and earned a promotion to Workshop Manager.

Ben is responsible for maintaining production levels and ensuring that the quality of materials, construction and finishing meet deVOL's extremely high standards, with no exceptions. Ben's unique blend of talents and experience are highly valued, and his creative input is regularly sought by the design team.

Ben’s impossibly broad knowledge of carpentry techniques and just about every type of wood there is made him a key part of the team when designing and making of our award-winning Sebastian Cox Kitchen range. Launched at Clerkenwell Design Week 2015, this kitchen has totally taken the design world by storm and has been awarded a Design Guild Mark as well as being named as Homes & Gardens ‘Kitchen Design of the Year’. Ben and the deVOL Design Team created a truly unique and innovative kitchen, something to be very proud of.

Ben's charming and unassuming nature endears him to all of our clients who clearly appreciate his attention to detail and his aesthetic viewpoint; he is a true asset to deVOL.

Whilst studying Furniture and Product Design at Nottingham Trent University, Matt designed a modular furniture system called 'ARRAY', which intended to challenge perceptions of furniture in a throw-away society as each design could be easily repaired or adapted to become usable in other pieces in the collection. The ARRAY Coffee Table was awarded the prestigious Innovation Award at the Young Furniture Makers' Awards 2018. 

Matt joined the deVOL team in 2018, two weeks before graduating from university. He is responsible for managing the manufacture and dispatch of all deVOL seating as well as helping with the development of our new Haberdasher’s Kitchen range. Matt has also been instrumental in setting up and running deVOL’s first 3D printer, helping to print a variety of components used in the casting of metalware and the development of other products too. 

Matt is really interested in traditional woodland crafts such as Windsor chair making, steam bending and spoon carving. He also still enjoys picking up a pen and sketching design ideas in his own time. Aside from design, Matt takes part in competitive shooting as part of the Nottinghamshire County Team for Small Bore Prone Target Rifle.

Dan graduated from Nottingham Trent University with a First Class Honours in Product Design. During his studies, Dan designed a multifunctional lamp and a folding lounge chair, both of which were imagined for small space living. Dan showcased his chair concept at the 2019 'Young Furniture Designers' exhibition and 'New Designers', where his work caught the eye of the deVOL team.

In the summer of 2019, Dan joined deVOL as a Product Designer, creating and developing new ideas for our ranges of furniture, lighting, ceramics and metalware, including the coveted Heirloom range. Dan has a keen interest in homeware and furniture, making him an ideal person for this important and varied role.

Outside of designing, Dan has a passion for sport and particularly enjoys playing and watching hockey and football.

Joe graduated from Nottingham Trent University in 2020 with a First Class Honours in Product Design. Throughout his degree he enjoyed designing intricate pieces of furniture and his final year project, a table which aimed to tackle working and dining in the same space, was awarded top place in the ‘Design for Humans’ category.

From a young age Joe had a keen interest in making and spent his early years building go-carts from scrap wood. At deVOL, Joe utilises his deep appreciation and understanding of various materials to make sure each one of our new designs functions at the highest level while looking unique and beautiful.

Outside of work, Joe enjoys playing music and getting out in nature. On the weekends you can find him cycling, trail running, and hiking.

Adam joined deVOL in 2022 after graduating with a First Class Honours in 3D Design (Furniture & Product). Whilst at university, Adam was shortlisted for multiple awards, including Made’s ‘Celebrating Extraordinary Design Award’ at New Designers and the Young Furniture Makers Design Award.

First starting in our metalware department, Adam became part of our product design team in 2023. Focusing primarily on projects for our metal studio, he enjoys thinking up new designs and manufacturing processes. No day is ever the same and Adam loves taking an idea from an initial sketch to a final prototype or production-ready product.

Outside of deVOL, Adam is a huge fan of motor sport, something that inspires much of his design work, and he can often be found in his shed, tinkering on a new build.

Finn studied Product Design and Technology at Loughborough University, where he focused particularly on electronics, combining technicality and function with beautiful aesthetics. For his final project, Finn created a motorcycle safety device that monitored behaviours whilst riding and provided live feedback using accelerometers and gyroscopes.

At deVOL, Finn’s role is very varied. A typical day may see him designing new products, whether that’s for our metalware and ceramics studios, or fresh ideas for our ever-growing and much-adored lighting and furniture ranges. Finn also helps to produce our existing products, making bespoke Gaselier Lights on the lathe at Cotes Mill and managing the production of our much-loved Frilly Glass Lights.

Outside of work, Finn is a keen sportsman, having played both cricket and football at a county level whilst growing up and competing in lacrosse and javelin. These days, Finn enjoys cycling with his deVOL colleagues, stopping off at lots of coffee shops along the way!

Lucy graduated from Nottingham Trent University in 2024 with a degree in Furniture and Product Design. During her studies, Lucy’s major project was a hand-carved wooden armchair, designed with a focus on sculptural form, comfort and tactile details. Lucy’s final year projects were selected to be showcased at New Designers and the Young Furniture Makers exhibition, and she was also invited to exhibit her armchair at an art gallery on Cork Street during London’s West End Gallery Night in 2024.

Joining deVOL in July 2025, Lucy is now part of our incredible team of product designers. Here, Lucy helps to research and create new home accessories to accompany our beautiful kitchens, focusing particularly on our much-loved lighting range.

Outside of work, Lucy enjoys sketching her own designs, exploring antique shops and markets, and working on her wood carving, making small models for friends.

With over 25 years of experience, Robin joined the deVOL team as Head of Finance in 2019. His previous roles saw him working in a variety of industries from FTSE 100 FMCG business to construction services to pharmaceuticals to civil engineering and even leisure.

During his time at deVOL Robin has been instrumental in supporting our finance department to keep up with the growth of the company, overseeing all financial matters both here in the UK and for our new venture in the USA. His strengths in financial modeling, as well as his ability to manage specific areas such as commercial, HR, pensions, risk and governance, have made him an invaluable member of the deVOL team. Robin particularly enjoys mentoring and coaching our finance team to give them the foundations to fulfill their potential.

When Robin's not at work, he enjoys spending time with his family and two very lively little dogs. He's a keen cyclist and sits on the committee of his local cycling club where he was, unsurprisingly, chosen to be treasurer.

After finishing her A-Levels, Milly spent a year working and travelling around Australia, New Zealand, Thailand and Laos, before coming home to work at a Gastro Pub where she quickly became the manager.

A short break in France to experience the ski season in Les Gets gave Milly the chance of a new environment. After returning from her ski season, Milly began working at another Gastro pub as a supervisor whilst saving for an AAT Accountancy Course, which she started in late 2012.

Milly quickly completed her course and is now a fully qualified AAT Accountant. Milly started working at deVOL in early 2013 as a Bookkeeper, working alongside Andrew to assist him with the day-to-day finances and accounts for deVOL Kitchens and also helping with the accounts for deVOL’s other companies; Shreddies and Floors of Stone.

As Milly has gained experience every aspect of her job at deVOL has become more in depth. She now manages deVOL’s payroll and works on month ends and year accounts for all of our companies.

In her spare time, Milly loves to go skiing and travel to experience new cultures. Extreme sports and water sports are also a passion as well as socialising with friends and family for drinks or nice meals out.

settings.staff_role: deVOL Shop Operations and Distribution Manager
settings.staff_description:
Lizzie joined the deVOL team shortly after graduating from Loughborough University in 2015 after developing a keen interest for interior design during her 3D Design degree.

Lizzie initially started working with both the production and design deVOL teams, allowing her to gain a better understanding of the full kitchen making process. 

Lizzie then moved on to become our Purchasing Manager which involves looking after the Purchasing team as a whole and ensuring everything from timber to appliances arrives on time.

She has gained a wealth of information over the years and has been able to build fantastic working relationships with our key suppliers.

At the weekend, you will find Lizzie outdoors or spending time with her family back in Yorkshire. In the colder months, you'll find her curled up with a good book, a cup of coffee and her cats, Luna and Monty.

Lucy joined deVOL in 2019 after graduating from Loughborough University, where she honed her skills in production planning and data analysis. She then went on to become a Homeware Buyer for Next, where her daily perusal for interiors inspiration first put deVOL on her radar.

Lucy is now one of our incredible Project Coordinators, so her day-to-day involves chatting to our customers and booking them in for site surveys, organising the delivery and installation of their kitchens, and managing our dispatch schedule.

Despite this busy timetable, Lucy finds the time to be our resident baker, frequently treating the team at Cotes Mill to delicious brownies! But when she’s not in the kitchen, Lucy can be found at the gym or walking her Hungarian Vizsla.

Chelsea joined deVOL in April 2023 as an Assistant Project Coordinator. This role is vital in ensuring every deVOL delivery and installation runs totally smoothly and to schedule. Day-to-day, Chelsea helps to manage the busy deVOL despatch calendar, books in site surveys and works with our customers to make sure their space is all ready for their lovely new furniture to arrive.

Outside of work Chelsea is an avid reader, and is fortunate enough to receive early-release copies of books from authors and publishers to review. When she’s not reading, you can find Chelsea at the theatre where she particularly enjoys watching musicals.

Alex graduated from the University of Nottingham in 2024 with a degree in Architectural Studies. Here, Alex fostered her technical drawing skills as well as exploring Environmental Science and Sustainable Urbanism modules. Alex is particularly proud of her dissertation, 'Unconsciously Living in Hostile Urban Environments and the Need to Consciously Fix Them', which explored the issue of Anti-Homeless architecture, with a case study on Nottingham City Centre

Joining deVOL in September 2024, assisting our project management team, Alex was quickly promoted to a Project Manager in 2025. In this role, Alex liaises with our customers from the final design stages through to the project sign-off and the installation of our lovely cabinetry. Alex is also responsible for carrying out site surveys, ensuring the project location is ready to receive furniture and appliances, so everything remains on schedule. 

When she’s not at deVOL, Alex pursues her passion for pottery and ceramics, having completed Level 1 and 2 Throwing courses at the Nottingham Ceramic School whilst she was at university. Alex also enjoys spending time travelling with friends and playing in a ladies' netball team.

Phil graduated from Loughborough University in 1988 and joined Insight Design Consultancy. He worked closely with Paul O'Leary on prototyping and was responsible for project administration and marketing insight's design services. Phil co-founded deVOL in 1989. Initially, much of the work involved furniture and architectural restoration which proved to be an excellent grounding in the traditionally accepted proportion and methods of construction.

Phil and Paul developed the deVOL style together over a period of ten years and built a reputation for delivering consistently high quality, cabinet made, freestanding kitchen furniture. Philip chose to take a sabbatical in 1998, but thankfully returned to take on the role of Customer Services Manager. Phil is renowned for being honest, fair and reliable which made him a natural for providing customer care. Phil also managed deVOL's sister company, deVOL Products, which sold decorative kitchen accessories and the deVOL Laundry Maid.

A few years ago, Phil and his wife, Claire, decided it was time for a new direction, and bought a 5 acre orange and olive farm in Portugal, with the long term vision of offering a spiritual retreat centre. Phil now works as deVOL’s Estate Project Manager, working on a wide variety of projects for deVOL. Phil continues to support the business, which he was so influential in nurturing, in a collaboration which has flourished for over 20 years.

A gentleman, a gifted artist, a friend, a colleague, a whirlwind of exuberance and fun.

Rhys came to deVOL in September 2015 and made an unforgettable impression on everyone he worked with.

He began his career at deVOL Cotes Mill and then moved to begin a life in London still working for deVOL. Every single person who met him, fell for his charm, they were smitten by his disarming ways and speechless of his limitless energy and enthusiasm for life.

Rhys tragically lost his life in a motorbike accident while in India on holiday in April 2019  and we want to keep him on our staff page, just to keep him in our thoughts and to remind us what a special person we all have lost.

His work friends in London have organised ‘A Picnic in the Park’ this summer and plan to celebrate Rhys in this way every year from now on.

In 2012 James travelled around Asia for 6 months before beginning a new job as a Project Manager at a construction company. Eager to see more of the world, James continued his travels for another 11 months in 2016 before joining deVOL as a Project Manager shortly after.

James managed our kitchen projects right through from the sale to the installation and ensured every single one ran smoothly. He liaised with customers on a daily basis, kept in constant touch with our kitchen design and production teams and made sure our customers were happy throughout every step of the kitchen manufacture, delivery and installation process.

A proud moment for James was exhibiting his handmade wooden furniture and accessories at both ‘Handmade in Kew’ and ‘Handmade in Chelsea’ and he hoped to take part in more national exhibitions in the future.

James was an expert climber and many of deVOL’s staff regularly climbed with him and he enjoyed, to the full, every social event.

James continued to work at Cotes Mill as a project manager until he was struck down with a rare and undetected stage 4 cancer in 2019. During his treatment, he only divulged his terrible situation to the Directors, preferring to be able to come to work and for everyone to be relaxed and chatting as usual, with no fuss or sympathy. Even laughing off people joking about how much holiday he was having.

He was grateful for our support and regularly chatted to Robin and me about his treatment and he pragmatically informed me of the chances of success. When all other treatment options had been exhausted, and there was just a slim chance of being accepted on a new trial drug, James was still unbelievably positive “Well, you’ve got to give it a go haven’t you, no matter how slim the chance.”

That was our last conversation; we hugged, and I hoped against hope that a miracle would happen. It was only 3 weeks later that we received the heart-breaking news from his newly married wife, Nicola, that James had lost his battle with cancer. When Robin announced to all the gathered staff at the Mill that James had passed away, they had no idea that he was that ill and I watched their faces break into horror, confusion and grief.

Everyone at deVOL knew James, everyone loved his cheerful and down to earth ways, and he made everyone laugh, even when he knew they might never see him again. I recognised the strongest human being I have ever met, and will probably ever meet, during those precious 6 months. They carried his coffin in to the sound of Wild Horses by the Rolling Stones and finished the service with Abba’s S.O.S. Having fun to the last, God bless a free spirit.

We will be creating a memorial to James in the grounds of Cotes Mill, for those of us who don’t want to forget.
